‘He knows’ - Fabian Hurzeler explains Pascal Gross and Brighton concern ahead of Conference League

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (423 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Fabian Hurzeler will let Pascal Gross decide if he needs a rest ahead of Brighton's clash with Craiova to the experienced midfielder himself.
  • The 35-year-old has been an ever-present for the Seagulls this season, starting all 18 of his appearances across the Premier League, Conference League and Carabao Cup.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fabian Hurzeler will let Pascal Gross decide if he needs a rest ahead of Brighton's clash with Craiova to the experienced midfielder himself.

The 35-year-old has been an ever-present for the Seagulls this season, starting all 18 of his appearances across the Premier League, Conference League and Carabao Cup.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Gross has accumulated 1,526 minutes of football in all competitions, underlining his importance to Hurzeler's side and the workload he has carried during the campaign.

The German midfielder has been key since returning to the Amex from Borussia Dortmund, but with Brighton facing another managing his fitness is becoming an increasingly notable consideration - especially with Newcastle at the Amex Stadium this Sunday,.

Hurzeler, speaking ahead of the meeting with Romanian league leaders Craiova, remarked: "We are in communication, and I think the only person who can really listen to himself is himself,” said the German.

"I know he's an experienced player, so if the time comes, we will have that conversation and, of course, make the decision.

"He's a clear team player, so if he feels he can't play at his highest level because of his physical condition or because he's tired in certain moments, then he will speak up.

"We have a very trusting relationship, so we will make the decision together.".

Gross has already demonstrated remarkable durability this season and whether Thursday's European fixture provides the moment for a rest remains to be seen.

Recent findings suggest that injuries will also play a factor in Hurzeler’s thinking. Malick Yalcouye is out for “several weeks” with a knee glitch and as yet, midfielder Mats Wieffer has not been added to the Conference League squad.

“I'm not really sure,” said Hurzeler to Sussex World when asked if they can include Wieffer and perhaps Yankuba Minteh to the Uefa list.

“We're trying to get an understanding of how things can work regarding this, but I can't say anything so far because we're still discussing what the best way to solve it is.

“He's definitely out for the next three Conference League games, but hopefully there's another possibility to replace him.”.

Diego Gomez and Olivier Boscagli are also sidelined for this one, while Chema Andres - who played in the 2-0 loss at Hull - is managing his fitness after withdrawing from Spain’s under-21 squad at the previous international break.

Yasin Ayari is also a midfield option for tonight.

Man Utd defender can 'pack his bags' in January as key Mauricio Pochettino transfer decision looms

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (401 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 08:07.
  • Noussair Mazraoui could be heading towards the Manchester United exit door when the January transfer window opens.
  • AC Milan are considering a move for the Morocco international as they look to strengthen their defensive options under former Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 25 Nov 2026 08:07.

Noussair Mazraoui could be heading towards the Manchester United exit door when the January transfer window opens.

AC Milan are considering a move for the Morocco international as they look to strengthen their defensive options under former Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim.

However, any potential departure will depend on Mauricio Pochettino's assessment of the 29-year-old over the coming weeks.

Mazraoui has experienced mixed fortunes since joining United from Bayern Munich, with injury problems restricting him to fewer than 1,000 Premier League minutes last season.

His fitness has improved this term, and he has featured six times in the league, partly because of injuries to United's other full-back options.

However, his long-term future at Old Trafford is now uncertain, with AC Milan reportedly keeping tabs on his situation.

According to reports in Italy (via Sport Witness), Milan have discussed Mazraoui's profile with their transfer team as they consider defensive reinforcements under Amorim.

The Portuguese coach has regularly used a back four this season and could view the United defender as an attractive option because of his ability to operate on either side.

There is reportedly a belief that Mazraoui could 'pack his bags in January', with the Serie A giants potentially open to pursuing a deal.

However, everything hinges on Pochettino's looks for the player. The Argentine is yet to make a final decision, with the next few weeks expected to help determine whether Mazraoui is allowed to leave.

United have several areas of the squad requiring attention, and selling Mazraoui could provide Pochettino with additional funds to work with in January.

The Argentine is believed to have a budget of just £50m, with the club expected to make only two additions unless significant circumstances change.

With central defence, left-back and striker all potential priorities, every extra contribution to the transfer kitty could prove valuable.

Mazraoui has not consistently established himself in one position at Old Trafford, and a departure could benefit all parties if Milan are prepared to offer a reasonable fee.

Industry observers note that united should not allow sentiment to get in the way of a sensible decision. If Pochettino does not see Mazraoui as an key part of his plans, cashing in during January could help fund reinforcements elsewhere.

There is still a decision to be made, but with multiple positions needing attention, every little helps.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As it stands, the Reds have two out-and-out strikers, Danilo Orsi and Pemi Aderoju, while Dylan Morgan, Ade Adeyemo and Stephen Duke-McKenna could all play in that role if needed.

Speaking after the Reds’ battling 0-0 draw with 2nd-placed Barnet on Tuesday night, which extended Blackwell’s unbeaten league record since he arrived, he stated “We tried to go with two strikers, but I’m not sure that game after game after game suits a couple of them.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Recent findings suggest that "I looked at the bench and there was nothing I could do. I tried to bring Osman (Kamara) to play up top and he naturally drifted out wide left and I didn’t want that.

“I wanted him to play as a two and he’s got to learn a lesson that when he goes on and he’s asked to do a job, do your job – and that’s what frustrates me a little bit.

"We didn’t have an actual sort of midfielder to come in and play. I think Dukey (Duke-McKenna) started to drift a little bit out to the right and I wanted him in alongside Kai, but once again, Dukey came in and did a job for me, pressed as hard as he could.

Sources indicate that “So, I can’t complain. It was a situation that if we’d remarked before the game that we’d remain unbeaten, you’d have been happy with that. So, we’re unbeaten and I’m happy with that.”.

Industry observers note that since Blackwell took over from Colin Kazim-Richards, Crawley have won two and drawn two, scoring four goals and conceding only two. The Reds are now level on points with Rotherham in 23rd with a game in hand, and only two points behind Rochdale in 22nd with two games in hand.

When asked if he has started looking at bringing anyone in to help out in the Janury transfer eindow, Blackwell said “To be fair, we were here from 12 o’clock today.

"We brought some newly introduced scouts in, a new recruitment guy and we had five hours today before the game kicked off looking at potential targets for January, and the club’s well on its way to do that.”.

While the Nye Camp boss concedes the Rocks will respect Elliot Powell’s side, he will ask his charges to concentrate on their own game plan in the Isthmian South Central division clash between the second-placed Channel Islanders and Bognor Regis Town, who are third.

Hollands’ men go into the keenly anticipated showdown on the back of a hard-fought 2-1 home win over an in-form Hayes & Yeading United outfit last time out.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Goals from Luke Roberts and Henry McDonald secured the victory and a vital three points that keep the home side in the reckoning at the top end of the standings — and Hollands believes a win is in his side’s grasp at the Springfield Stadium.

Industry observers note that he told the club’s official YouTube channel: “We’ve got to worry about ourselves more so than we do Jersey. We will obviously pay them respect; we're going to their home ground and they're doing well so you have to pay the respect.

“But we must make sure that we have a plan suitable for us to get three points away from home, which will be a tough ask — but it's something that I feel we can achieve if we play to the heights that we have done this season.

“We have to have belief because we have shown that on our day we can compete with some of the best teams in this division.

It has been revealed that “I've got belief in them. It's all about what we can do and how we can influence games. I feel if we turn up, then we can compete with anyone, but we have to show that and have to do so on a more consistent basis.”.

The most recent triumph — which came after a home win over Littlehampton Town — further addressed a mini-slump in the league and the gaffer states his charges should take the positives from getting back on track.

He added: “We must take the positives from two league wins on the spin and make sure we go there (Jersey) with the confidence that provides.”.

*The club estimates the number of travelling Rocks fans attending the game will be around 400, an incredible following for step 4 football.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Mikel Arteta remarked David Raya’s shoulder injury isn’t ‘too serious’, sparking hope that the goalkeeper could return within weeks.
  • Raya was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle on Saturday at St James’ Park, hurting his left shoulder in a collision with William Osula.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ISAAN KHAN, REPORTER and WILL GRIFFEE.

Published: 09:10 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:39 EST, 24 November 2026.

Mikel Arteta remarked David Raya’s shoulder injury isn’t ‘too serious’, sparking hope that the goalkeeper could return within weeks.

Raya was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle on Saturday at St James’ Park, hurting his left shoulder in a collision with William Osula. He looked in agony as he left the pitch.

His No 2 Kepa Arrizabalaga is instead expected to play for the north London club in their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday.

Though Arteta confirmed Raya doesn’t require surgery and didn’t yet rule him out for Sunday’s Premier League clash against Manchester City.

Sources indicate that ‘He’s (Raya) not fit for tomorrow, but it doesn’t look too serious,’ noted Arteta. ‘We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. It seems to be better than expected.

‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first test shows something much more encouraging.

Arsenal's No 1 David Raya underwent an MRI scan the day after going off against Newcastle.

‘There is no need for surgery, which was the main fear because that would have ruled him out for months.’.

Asked whether Raya could play at home to Man City, he added: ‘Tomorrow we’ll have more tests and we will know. I think we’ve seen what David brings to the team as well.

Sources indicate that ‘That’s why we are very protective with Kepa and (third-choice) Illan (Meslier). Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen.’.

Raya has been sensational for the Premier League champions and his absence is likely to hurt the best defensive unit.

According to recent reports, 'That's a massive worry,' Ian Wright stated on Sky Sports when the stopper went down. 'I don't want to say I'm petrified simply because Kepa is in goal, he's the guy who has got to try and keep the goals out for us now.

In a recent development, 'But yeah, that is a massive blow. Someone like him, Declan Rice, Gabriel, it is very tough to replace those guys.'.

Meanwhile, Bruno Guimaraes said Arteta is ‘crazy’ about the small details that will take him to ‘another level’.

Since his summer move from Newcastle, the 29-year-old has scored vital goals against Sunderland and Leeds - but is yet to complete a full 90 minutes in the Premier League.

Raya hit the turf in pain and went off the pitch clutching his arm to indicate that something serious had happened.

‘I now definitely understand my role in the team and the way Mikel wants me to play but I can still play much better,’ stated the Brazilian.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I think Mikel (Arteta) is unbelievable. He as a manager is so focused on small details, the way you control the ball, the way that you cannot be aligned with your opposite side.

‘Some details I have never heard before, I just found out with him here. He is crazy a little bit about these small details and I try and take (in) as much as I can because he is so passionate about them.

In a recent development, ‘He highlighted me some clips (from when I was) in Newcastle and some clips here, where he thinks I can do things differently. He's trying to take me to another level.’.

Sources indicate that arsenal's clash with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night will feature a new innovation for its TV audience watching on Prime Video. Called 'Progressive Actions' it highlights the passes and ball carries that drive a team up the pitch, and the often-unsung players behind them. Developed by Prime Video's team of producers, engineers, AI experts, and on-air analysts, Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built specifically for the UEFA Champions League. It joins the growing suite of features on Prime Vision, the alternate feed which serves as a laboratory and incubator for new features that often advance to the main broadcast.

It has been revealed that progressive Actions is built on proprietary AI-powered models that identify a Progressive Action based on how far the ball travels in each phase of the pitch, with the threshold becoming shorter closer to the opposition goal where defences are more compact and space is harder to find. The metric mirrors the data used behind the scenes at Europe's elite clubs, yet has historically been difficult to show during a live broadcast. As a player makes a Progressive Action, an on-pitch graphic will show where the action started and ended, the player involved, and the distance the ball advanced, allowing fans to see the game as a coaching team would, in real time.

'Prime Vision is where we develop latest features that shine a spotlight on the metrics, actions and players that impact a game most, yet aren't always captured by traditional statistics or broadcast techniques,' remarked Andrew Hornett, Director of Live Sports Production for Europe at Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that 'Every team has players whose influence goes far beyond the scoresheet, the ones doing the crucial work in the build-up, moving the ball forward two or three passes before an assist. Progressive Actions is designed to capture that impact, measuring and visualising these actions during a live broadcast. Fans will see them in real time as they happen, but we'll also aggregate the data across the game, so you can see which players have had the biggest impact on the match.'.

Recent findings suggest that the feature will debut in the UK and Ireland on Tuesday and will also be available for fans in Germany and Italy. Fans can access Prime Vision, with features including Progressive Actions, via their remote from the match detail page or the in-game menu during any live UCL fixture on Prime Video.

Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built from the ground up specifically for Prime Video's UEFA Champions League coverage, and sits alongside Tactical Map, Momentum, Physical Insights, Advanced Analytics, Passing Options, and Player ID in Prime Vision's growing suite of features designed to take football fans closer to the game, all available on the alternate feed during every UEFA Champions League match live on Prime Video. Prime Insights were first developed for Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football, its exclusive weekly NFL package in the US, where AI-powered features including the award-winning Defensive Alerts have become a staple of the coverage, advancing from the alternate feed to the main broadcast each week.

Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5473 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under newly introduced head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
  • On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under newly introduced head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Sources indicate that mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he demonstrated during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Sources indicate that for Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

It has been revealed that “I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

In a recent development, liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

Recent findings suggest that as does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

It has been revealed that there was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Industry observers note that we knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

According to recent reports, atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

According to recent reports, the question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

According to recent reports, “I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:.

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a newly introduced contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

Sources indicate that “I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

It has been revealed that the Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what substantial clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very key.”.

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola remarked. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a substantial challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

Sources indicate that “It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a major responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

Atletico Madrid at the moment sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

After Ashley Nathaniel-George cancelled out Roy Syla’s opener just before half-time, a five minute spree including two goals from John Marquis and an own-goal from Harvey Griffiths turned the tide heavily in favour of the hosts after the interval.

Dominic Johnson-Fisher’s superb showing from the bench brought the Rebels within touching distance of leaving Surrey with a point after the number nine netted twice, but the deficit could not be overturned before the full-time whistle.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It was the hosts who enjoyed the better start of the two side through 20 minutes, as experienced forward Marquis had two sights on goal early on. A driving run down the right flank by Jaiden Putman inside the first minute led to the former Portsmouth striker being picked out at the far post, yet he could not get an effort away under pressure from multiple Worthing bodies.

Five minutes later, another breakaway for the Cardinals saw Marquis latch onto a lofted ball in behind the Rebels backline. Shaping onto his left side, the 34 year-old’s strike was kept out by the midriff of Harrison Foulkes.

Worthing had spells of promise during the early exchanges, with the weekend’s match-winner Jordan Young instrumental once again in most of the away side’s attacking play. The former Torquay United man had his best effort of the half just after quarter of an hour, linking up with Kendall through the right channel before firing over Vicente Reyes’ crossbar.

Putman’s adventurous play down the Woking right posed a persistent threat to the left of the visitors’ defence throughout the first half. The QPR-loanee tested Foulkes with an attempt of his own with 20 minutes on the clock drifting inward from the right side before being kept out by another Foulkes intervention.

With half an hour on the clock, a double substitution from Hinshelwood to bring on both Cory Adjetey-Brew and Nathaniel-George proved the spark for a crescendo of action to close out the half.

A loose ball following an aerial challenge allowed Putman to drive forward down the right. The ball found the feet of Josh Kelly at the by-line, who swivelled before picking out the run of Syla into the box. With Syla unmarked, the midfielder side-footed the ball past Foulkes to open the scoring.

Recent findings suggest that woking’s first half advantage did not last long, and it was one of the two first half changes in Nathaniel-George who fashioned an equaliser with a minute of normal time remaining in the period. Cutting in from the left flank, the substitute curled a right-footed strike which nestled into Reyes’ bottom left corner from 20 yards out. A spectacular way to open his goalscoring account for the Rebels.

While Worthing’s rapid response may have spurned optimism amongst the travelling faithful heading into the break, the start of the second half spelled nothing but turmoil from a Worthing perspective.

Less than a minute after play resumed, Marquis notched his second of the night after turning the ball home from the edge of the six-yard box with a flicked finish amidst a sea of away defenders.

The hosts doubled their advantage almost immediately after regaining their lead. A poorly-executed pass from Foulkes invited Woking to spring an attack, and with the visitors’ keeper stranded off his goal-line, Marquis swept home into an empty net to make it 3-1.

Sources indicate that five minutes of horror to start the half culminated with the home side adding a fourth goal. Another giveaway in midfield presented Josh Grant the opportunity to drive towards the box. Grant’s eventual effort fizzed off the foot of the retreating Griffiths, with Foulkes helpless to watch the ball trickle over the line.

Recent findings suggest that the away contingent stunned following a flurry of concessions, Hinshelwood looked to the bench yet again for inspiration in giving the Rebels a chance of coming away with something. One of those introductions was Johnson-Fisher, who netted two brilliant goals to bring the visitors back to within one.

It has been revealed that in the 64th minute, a ball in from the left side was brought down astutely by the former Whitehawk striker, who fired the ball home on the turn off the underside of the crossbar. Then, 12 minutes later, another fine finish from Johnson-Fisher gave Worthing their third, this time getting on the end of a low pass in behind from Nathaniel-George before slotting a low drive underneath the body of Reyes.

In a recent development, ultimately, despite the visitors’ best efforts in the closing stages. three goals in rapid succession to start the second half proved too much for the away side to overcome on a cold Tuesday night of madness at the Kingfield Stadium.

This one was not a match for the football connoisseur – but was one for fans of never-say-die defending as Broadbridge Heath put on a tenacious display of defending against promotion hopefuls Erith Town on a bitter cold Tuesday evening at the JM Clark Stadium.

Chris Simmons’ Heath side knew it would be a difficult match up against a Dockers side on top form, second in the division with games in-hand and with the best home record in the division having played eight and won all eight.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But it was the Bears who had the first shot on target on 9 minutes when Sam Hards was brought down some 30 yards from goal and Ben Royall stepped up to take the resulting free-kick – hitting a left foot shot that was saved comfortably low to his left by the Dockers goalkeeper Javern Pitterson.

On 16 minutes Erith were awarded a free-kick wide on the right and just outside the penalty area, James Dyer played the ball into the danger area where it pinged in and around the 6 yard box before being cleared by Brad Peters and that set the tone for the first half with the hosts having most of the play but unable to break down the solid Bears defence.

Broadbridge Heath did have a few chances, Royall tried to catch Pitterson out with a shot to the near-post but the keeper got back to gather and Ollie Rawlins had a left foot shot saved by Pitterson diving low to his left and it was 0-0 at the break.

The Dockers stepped up a gear in the second half, kicking down the slope, and had the Bears pinned back in their own half for long periods but without really troubling goalkeeper Alfie Hadfield, plenty of goal attempts but everyone charged down by a Broadbridge Heath player defending like their lives depended on it.

On 75 minutes a rare foray deep into the Erith half saw Charlie Connell brought down by a clumsy challenge some 25 yards from goal, Ben Royal stepped up to take the resulting free-kick striking a left foot shot that deflected off the wall wrong-footing Pitterson who could do nothing but watch the ball fly into the net out of his reach.

The hosts continued to push players forward in search of an equaliser but just couldn’t get past the Broadbridge Heath defensive lines who stood firm and dealt with everything the Dockers could throw at them – and it remained 0-1 at the final whistle with Heath continuing their remarkable run of having scored in every league game this season.

Simmons stated afterwards: “This one was a bit of a smash and grab, Erith are a very good side and should of gone in front in the first half, defensively we were excellent and our shape and organisation was top notch and in the end got the lucky break the lads deserved.”.

Next up for the Bears is the visit of division leaders Faversham Town to the Air Engineering Stadium on Saturday.

BBH: Hadfield, Cotton, Royall, Marino, Peters, Richardson, Connell, Bejashvili (Doughty 71), Rawlins, Holden, Hards.

AC Milan are five points behind the somewhat surprise league-leaders Lazio, but belief is growing regarding a Scudetto push.

Industry observers note that as La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Milan re-emerged from the two-week international break and put in arguably their best performance of the season against Frosinone. They scored five goals and it could have been more, racking up a third league win in a row to move back into the top four.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The table remains quite tight at the top, with Inter the only team to slip up over the weekend, and the Rossoneri are firmly in the running. The paper highlights give reasons that a title fight is very possible.

Industry observers note that gerry Cardinale and Ruben Amorim are inextricably linked, and that might seem obvious, given that one is the owner and the other the coach. In reality, the bond is deeper than usual, for one simple reason.

In a recent development, amorim has been handed the keys to create the ‘new Milan’, one that Cardinale has decided to manage completely differently since the end of May. The Portuguese is the coach to whom RedBird have given the longest contract so far, and Cardinale believes he’s the right man at the right time.

According to recent reports, he’s demonstrating this concretely not only with his constant presence and his reassuring words, but also with his intention to improve the squad quickly and with the arrival of a key management figure like Markus Krösche. Now, Amorim will receive even greater support.

It has been revealed that gonçalo Inacio, Nicolo Tresoldi, Endrick. These are just some of the names circulating – and these aren’t rumours, but actual targets – ahead of a potentially crucial January transfer window.

The question is obvious: with a couple of top-notch signings for the second half of the season, how far could this team go? Staying up there for starters remains the minimum objective, with Champions League football a must.

Industry observers note that then, Amorim and co. hope that the rest will follow, if their rivals begin to lose pace. The coach is starting to make his team look like they are clicking, but Cardinale has realised the need to accelerate to fill the remaining gaps in the squad.

Recent findings suggest that amorim (fortunately) rapidly realised that the average tactical level of his colleagues in Italy is too high to allow himself to present his Milan team in the same way every single way. So, the 3-4-2-1 that was previously seemingly set in stone has become plasticine in his hands.

The manager moulds and shapes the playing system based on the opponents, rather than his own needs. Since Ruben the fundamentalist became Ruben the quick-change artist, we’ve seen a bit of everything: 4-2-3-1, 4-3-3, 4-4-1-1, 3-5-2.

The former Sporting CP coach coach locks himself in the lab throughout the week and tailors the formation he deems best. Sometimes he gets it wrong, but most of the time he gets it right.

In a recent development, milan have won five of their last six league games and, game by game, they are increasingly able to camouflage themselves effectively tactically. Opponents never know what formation they will face, while Amorim has several players capable of playing well in multiple roles, which helps.

The data is remarkable and reads as follows: only Rocco (29) and Czeizler (31) coached Milan sides that have scored more goals than Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 Serie A games in charge.

In short, despite all the problems involved (Goncalo Ramos in particular, more on him to come) the coach’s attacking vocation is clearly visible. Furthermore, it is a Milan with a high conversion rate in proportion to the shots on target.

Industry observers note that it is also a Diavolo side that have somehow found a way to make up for Ramos’ poor contribution in terms of goals. Alphadjo Cisse, Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot take turns to set each other up and score, a sign of a growing offensive physiognomy.

In a recent development, more often than not, a striker simply needs to get a goal in order to build confidence and then begin a virtuous cycle. Milan hope that this is the case for Ramos, who ended his month-long goal drought on Sunday.

However, the reflection goes further: while the Rossoneri having the luxury of being able to score without goals from their No.9 (who is at the moment on three in the league), surely things can only get better from here?

In short, if the Portuguese international actually does start firing more regularly, then Milan might unlock another dimension to their attack that could really see them surge towards that elusive Scudetto.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 09:50.
  • Real Madrid thrashed PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday night and are growing in strength this season, thanks to the work of Jose Mourinho and the form of several players.
  • Thierry Henry's words on CBS on Tuesday night sum up the feeling that is starting to emerge around Real Madrid:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 09:50.

Real Madrid thrashed PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday night and are growing in strength this season, thanks to the work of Jose Mourinho and the form of several players.

Thierry Henry's words on CBS on Tuesday night sum up the feeling that is starting to emerge around Real Madrid:.

In a recent development, 'Real Madrid played an exceptional game. Playing like that, they are serious contenders for the Champions League. They are improving enormously from week to week. Something is going on at Real Madrid, watch out!'.

After a start to the season marked by some turbulence, Real Madrid appear to have found their cruising speed. The spectacular win over PSV Eindhoven (5-1) in the Champions League confirmed that impression. Mourinho's side have just strung together a tenth consecutive victory in all competitions and have a perfect record in the Champions League, with five wins from five games. Above all, Real Madrid seem to have taken a step forward in their ability to turn games around.

The script against the Dutch side was far from straightforward. Trailing at half-time after a particularly worrying first half, Real Madrid looked a completely different team after the break. It was a reaction that bore the signature of their manager, who made three changes at half-time.

The other big positive of the evening was Jude Bellingham. Left on the bench at kick-off, the Englishman made a sensational entrance at half-time, to the point of transforming his side. His work rate, ability to get forward and influence between the lines immediately gave Real Madrid more options. His superb goal, scored after a remarkable piece of skill, rewarded a top-class performance.

Thierry Henry, again, was full of admiration:.

In a recent development, '(Jude) Bellingham is incredible, the way he plays. Wearing the number 5 at Real Madrid is not easy, but he does it with astonishing ease. His personality is extraordinary. I cannot believe that some people doubted him in his own country. But he has silenced the sceptics with his current performances and proved to them that they were wrong at the World Cup. He always delivers with his attitude and his play.'.

Beyond his statistics, with seven goals and five assists in 18 appearances, Bellingham brings an extra dimension to Real Madrid's midfield. Mourinho therefore has a player capable of turning a game, but also of giving a real identity to the side's attacking play.

The Englishman's performance should not, however, overshadow Mourinho's decisions. At half-time, the Portuguese made a bold call with three changes: Bellingham, Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen replaced Aurelien Tchouameni, Antonio Rudiger and Eder Militao. It was a spectacular reshuffle, particularly at centre-back, where the two starters were punished after a difficult first half.

Recent findings suggest that but there was also a desire to rebalance the side behind this choice. By installing Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva in midfield, Mourinho prioritised technical control and ball circulation. Real Madrid were able to push their block up, press higher and regain control of the game. The manager also explained that he used several video clips during the break to correct his players' defensive and attacking mistakes.

According to Jamie Carragher on CBS:.

In a recent development, 'Mourinho is building a fantastic team. Week after week, we see them improving. They lost to Atletico Madrid and we thought the season was over, but they managed to pull themselves together by beating Barcelona' - Carragher said.

The Hornets were beaten 2-1 in Kent on Saturday before picking up an excellent 1-0 home success against the high-flying Tinners in midweek.

Horsham took the lead in their visit to Dover but came away empty-handed.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Charlie Hester-Cook gave them an early advantage but Euan Williams levelled promptly. Ruben Soares-Junior’s second half goal proved the hosts’ winner.

Lee Harding was then sent off late on for a second yellow card offence.

Sources indicate that di Paola told us: “I don’t think we played particularly well. I can’t argue with the scoreline. There are no real arguments, really. I think they were the better team.

In a recent development, “The pitch meant you couldn’t really play any football, but that suited them. I’m not a football snob. There’s no wrong or right way of playing football. The way they play is effective and works for them.

In a recent development, “It’s not a vanity contest, it’s a winning games contest and they beat us. I’ve no complaints with the result, I just don’t enjoy watching that kind of football.

Recent findings suggest that “We tried to play the same way as them but we weren’t brave enough and it played into their hands. They were always going to be better at that kind of football than us.

Sources indicate that “We weren’t great but we weren’t bad either. They had three shots, we had three shots, they scored two of them, we scored one of them.

“I wasn’t that frustrated, angry or disappointed after the game, I just felt we didn’t have the right amount of intensity – and it’s not the kind of place you can go without an intent to battle and fight.”.

Horsham then became the first side to defeat second-placed Truro in National League South since mid-September.

Reece Myles-Meekums’ 16th minute strike proved to be the difference between the two sides. The win leaves the Hornets 14th in the table.

Di Paola added: “If either them or Ebbsfleet don’t win the league then I couldn’t tell you who would. They’re by far and away the best two teams we’ve played.

It has been revealed that “We had to suffer but we suffered as a unit. I don’t think Michael [Dike] had loads to do in goal. He made one good save but in general he was sweeping and tidying up.

Industry observers note that “The game would have been made much easier if Nadders [Ashley Nadesan] had scored his one-on-one in the second half. It would have taken the game away from them – but if you don’t score the second you have to suffer.

“That’s something we know we have to do better at, putting teams away. But it’s such a hard league.

“It was always going to be a huge challenge. I don’t think Truro had lost in a couple of months. They’re a top, top side, so to collect a win was really pleasing.”.

Meanwhile, goalkeeper Sam Howes has had his contract cancelled by the Hornets. His departure has seen the return of young Brighton stopper Dike on a 28-day loan.

Horsham travel to sixth-placed Billericay Town this Saturday – and Di Paola revealed a number of his midfielders were stricken going into the the trip to Essex.

Recent findings suggest that he noted: “Everyone’s on their backsides at the moment! Ronan [Silva] is a doubt. He’s been so unlucky. He took a bash to his ankle [against Truro] and it swelled up. It’s not his hamstring, which is one good thing.

“Charlie played injured against Truro because we needed him – but those are the kinds of boys we want at the football club.”.

Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5336 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.
  • According to recent reports, memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions.
  • Industry observers note that thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

According to recent reports, memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Industry observers note that thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

Industry observers note that in five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”.

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Sources indicate that their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” remarked Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”.

Recent findings suggest that there was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

Sources indicate that to lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r.

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm.

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN.

"We missed so many substantial chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH.

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Wed, October 21: Bayern Munich (A) 8pm.

Wed, November 4: Slavia Prague (A) 8pm.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm.

Wed, December 9: Real Madrid (H) 8pm.

Wed, January 20: Real Betis (A) 8pm.

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” noted Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”.

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

Recent findings suggest that “He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”.

Recent findings suggest that couple that with his impressive chemistry with upcoming arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star signs newly introduced lucrative deal, writes MATT BARLOW

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1314 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.
  • De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026.

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

Williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old said he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

According to recent reports, this is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. On Tuesday, he was rewarded for his progress with a fresh contract at the club.

He said: 'This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight.

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals.

'Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

'The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.'.

Sources indicate that hopes are indeed high. Similarities with Yamal are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No 10 position.

He does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

His brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Here, they rose to salute a latest talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

The Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' mentioned De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

The 18-year-old had rival clubs circling but Spurs have now tied him down.

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side.

Sources indicate that spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Williams-Barnett was under contract until 2028 but his new deal means clubs circling must now look elsewhere.

It is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping problems but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

Although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' noted De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and stated it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley, and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

Industry observers note that there was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

The pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

On the upcoming deal, thought to be for five years, the manager remarked: 'Luca is a player I think the world of, and I'm so happy that he has signed a new contract.

'He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

'Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

Sources indicate that 'The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.'.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 10:10.
  • Southampton and Middlesbrough square off at St Mary's on Friday night in their first showdown since the conclusion of the Spygate saga.
  • While the visitors sit at the top of the Championship table, the Saints are just seven points adrift of opponents who are now viewed as one of their fierce rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 10:10.

Southampton and Middlesbrough square off at St Mary's on Friday night in their first showdown since the conclusion of the Spygate saga.

While the visitors sit at the top of the Championship table, the Saints are just seven points adrift of opponents who are now viewed as one of their fierce rivals.

More than six months on from Tonda Eckert being found guilty of launching a spying mission on a Middlesbrough training session ahead of their playoff semi-final, Southampton have moved on from the controversy that rocked English football.

While Eckert will accept the attention that Friday's game attracts, he will remain focused on trying to secure promotion to the Premier League.

Despite being docked four points as part of their punishment from the Football Association, Southampton can move to within four points of Boro with victory on the South coast.

That noted, the Saints have struggled for consistency of late, only collecting five points from four games and conceding a late equaliser to draw 1-1 at Sheffield United on Tuesday night.

According to recent reports, nevertheless, Southampton have been sensational at their home ground. Not only have 22 points being accumulated from a possible 24, they have scored 22 goals and conceded just five.

As for Middlesbrough, they make the long trip south having collected 12 points from eight fixtures, albeit only prevailing on three occasions.

Eight goals had been scored in back-to-back away successes at Stoke City and Bolton Wanderers, yet Kim Hellberg's side have failed to score in the last two such contests versus Wrexham and Watford.

However, 2-0 and 2-1 successes over Bristol City and Swansea City at the Riverside Stadium have ensured that Boro enter this game in top spot with 34 goals from their 17 matches.

Will Lankshear's return from a minor injury may also prove key. Despite being limited to a 62-minute outing versus Swansea, he netted his 14th Championship goal of the season.

Middlesbrough Championship form:.

Eckert will recall a number of his Southampton regulars for this contest, with Jack Stephens, Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz among those who will start.

James Bree may also feature on the back of his 30-minute outing versus Sheffield United after a minor injury, but Leo Scienza is likely to be named on the substitutes' bench at best after missing the last two matches.

Centre-back Keven Schlotterbeck will be sidelined until December through injury.

As for Boro, Sebastian Berhalter is expected to return in central midfield, with Myles Peart-Harris potentially being used further forward.

Providing that Lankshear demonstrates no ill-effects from Tuesday's game, he should start, with David Strelec likely dropping down to the bench to accommodate an extra midfielder.

Despite concerns over an ankle injury, Neto Borges came through 90 minutes versus Swansea and seems in line to be selected at left-back.

Southampton possible starting lineup:.

Peretz; Roerslav, Abbott, Stephens, Manning; Downes, Ward-Prowse; Matsuki, Azaz, Dobbin; Larin.

Middlesbrough possible starting lineup:.

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Borges; Morris, Berhalter; Cozier-Duberry, Peart-Harris, McGree; Lankshear.

Although Boro have returned from the November international break with back-to-back wins, we cannot ignore the intensity that these two teams will play at during this contest. That, and home advantage, may favour Southampton, leading us to predict a narrow victory for Eckert's side in a game that will include plenty of cautions.

“I think Ramsgate definitely deserved to win,” stated Altendorff. “Maybe the scoreline flatters them slightly, but I would say that the end result is justified. We weren't our best.

“Ramsgate were playing a very direct brand of football. We found it difficult to cope with. We didn't win enough first and second contacts, especially in the first half. They got what they deserved, and so did we.”.

On a punishing afternoon for the Rooks, heavy first-half pressure led to a fine brace from TJ Jadama, while it could have been worse with another strike rattling the crossbar.

Lewes struggled to escape their half, with Charlie Walker on the end of some contentious decisions as he tried to break away as the sole outlet for much of the match.

While Alfie Allen’s 68th-minute header offered the Rooks some hope, and a quadruple substitution injected some intent, a fourth Ramsgate goal in added time knocked the stuffing out of Lewes.

“The scoreline enabled us to try something different because at that stage of the game, it's already three nil to them,” remarked Altendorff. “We did actually improve. The boys off the bench did well when they came on.

“I thought Tyler Christian-Law was excellent and added a bit of bite to midfield. We didn't seem to lack anything by withdrawing a third midfielder. If anything, we looked even more threatening.

“Even towards the end of the game, Charlie had a good opportunity to put one in the back of the net from six yards out. Unfortunately, it just wasn't our day. Nothing seemed to fall for us.”.

Lewes have now won just one of their last seven Isthmian Premier Division matches and face a tricky test at 7th-placed Leatherhead this Saturday.

Just as Ramsgate were last weekend, the Surrey side are three points behind the Rooks with a game in hand and a superior goal difference, meaning they can leapfrog Lewes with a win.

On Tuesday night, Leatherhead beat Ramsgate 1-0 at home to move into the play-off places, but with this being their first win in four games, the Ian Selley-led side are not in electric form either.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the former England striker, turned broadcaster, was discussing Fabian Hürzeler's side on The Rest is Football podcast – following Albion’s disappointing 2-0 defeat at Hull City. A victory would have taken the high-flying Seagulls to within three points to leaders Arsenal.

Sources indicate that brighton produced some impressive football but were unable to find a way past an inspired opposition goalkeeper, in Konstantinos Tzolakis. Their failure to convert chances proved costly, with Oli McBurnie stealing the game with a late brace.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Sources indicate that despite the result, Lineker was left hugely impressed by what he saw from the Seagulls. He described Brighton as the ‘best team to watch in the league’ when it comes to the quality of football.

The former Tottenham and Barcelona striker stated he believes the addition of a clinical centre-forward could make Albion a formidable proposition.

"If Brighton had a nine like Leicester had in Jamie Vardy, I think they would be serious title challengers," Lineker, 65, noted.

Recent findings suggest that "They create so many chances. They haven't got, or at least I've not seen, a real nine in there that sniffs out [goals].".

The former Match of the Day host acknowledged that the Seagulls had played some excellent football but could not find the finishing touch.

"I watched the Brighton game yesterday, and I still can't quite work out [how they didn’t score]," he remarked.

"Well, I can, because they missed too many chances, and the opposition's keeper was unbelievable, but they played some incredibly good football.

"They couldn't score, which is unusual because they've scored more goals than any other team in the league this season.

"Even though they lost 2-0, I was thinking, God, Brighton are good.

"I go back to the point but if they had someone like a Vardy, wow, they'd be very difficult to stop, I think.".

Regardless, Lineker said he ‘definitely can see’ Brighton in the Champions League next season.

His fellow podcast pundit Micah Richards agreed with the assessment. But he also felt the result was particularly damaging to Brighton's ambitions.

The former Manchester City full-back suggested that, if the Seagulls were serious about making a push towards the top of the Premier League, winning at Hull was essential.

"I know it's ridiculous – and we're talking about jumping on the bandwagon and being reactionary – but I think for a real push, they had to win that game," he said.

However, Richards, 38, was equally complimentary about the football Hürzeler's team are producing.

"I think they play some of the best football in the Premier League – they create so many chances," he said.

According to recent reports, he agreed that they ideally need to sign a prolific number nine. But he was keen to stress that the comments were not intended as criticism of Albion’s current forwards – including Georginio Rutter, who started the match at Hull, and Charalampos Kostoulas.

"It's no disrespect to Rutter, he's just not got the clinical edge of a world-class player," Richards explained.

Richards also highlighted the contribution of midfielder Yasin Ayari, particularly his ability to make late runs into the penalty area.

Alan Shearer was another to praise Brighton's performance, describing the quality of their football and the pace at which they moved the ball.

Recent findings suggest that "Great football, some brilliant football. They were passing and moving at pace – superb," the all-time leading Premier League goalscorer said.

The Newcastle legend added: "It was just one of those days where the keeper had his day and nothing was going to go past him. You have that and you just move on.”.

Shearer, 56, also felt the result should not overshadow the quality of Brighton's display.

"I think he [Hürzeler] will be disappointed with the result, but performance-wise, I thought they were brilliant,” he said.

Brighton were not the only team to receive praise, with Richards also highlighting Bournemouth's recent formidable form.

The podcast trio agreed that the quality across the Premier League is improving, with Richards arguing that teams outside the traditional 'big six' are becoming increasingly difficult opponents.

In a recent development, for Brighton, however, Lineker's message was clear. He believes Hürzeler has a side capable of playing some of the best football in the country, but adding a striker with the instincts and finishing ability of Vardy could make them a much more dangerous proposition.

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 11:02.

On Tuesday night, in Dakar, it was possible to seriously imagine Ismaila Sarr lifting the African Ballon d'Or. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) had just confirmed Senegal's triumph at the Africa Cup of Nations, and the Crystal Palace winger saw his candidacy significantly strengthened.

Sources indicate that yet the next day, his name had disappeared from the list. The Confederation of African Football (CAF) selected Sadio Mane and Pape Gueye on the Senegalese side, along with Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari for Morocco.
