A winner of the Conference League with Crystal Palace, Sarr also finished as the competition's top scorer with nine goals and was named the best player of the tournament.

Sources indicate that at the World Cup, he scored four times, including a goal against Belgium in the round of 32. He has a total of 24 goals and five assists in 53 games in 2026, for club and country. That annual record goes beyond the period assessed by CAF, which ended on 15 September. His European title and his World Cup, however, fell within that window, as did the Africa Cup of Nations triumph, even though its validation only came after the fact.

Pape Gueye scored the goal that won the Africa Cup of Nations for Senegal and features in the team of the tournament. Sadio Mane, the winner in 2019 and 2022, was named the best player of this Africa Cup of Nations. Their places are defensible.

But if the three Senegalese had to be separated over the whole period, Sarr's case, decisive at club level and at the World Cup, appears more complete. He had what it took to aim for first place. Seeing him miss out on the top five is hard to understand.

Recent findings suggest that the CAS ruling revived that hope in Senegal when voting had already closed. CAF had set the end of voting for 20 November, four days before the verdict.

In a recent development, achraf Hakimi remains the favourite among the five selected. The 2025 winner, the full-back won a second consecutive Champions League with Paris Saint-Germain and reached the World Cup quarter-finals with Morocco.

In a recent development, brahim Diaz finished as the top scorer at the Africa Cup of Nations with five goals. His missed Panenka in the final remains the most striking image of his tournament, after he had found the net in five games in a row.

Industry observers note that ismael Saibari, meanwhile, scored against Brazil, Scotland and Haiti. He became the first African to score in each of his country's three group games at a single World Cup. Currently injured, the Bayern player can therefore also hope for a crowning at the ceremony on 2 December in Lagos.

Those at the top of the club must do the same this winter and take accountability if the beleaguered Oakwell outfit are to have any chance of getting out of the mess they are in and avoid playing fourth-tier football next season for the first time since 1978-79.

It has been revealed that on the pitch at Valley Parade, it was a rinse-and-repeat performance from the Reds, who outperformed Bradford in attacking metrics, just as they did to Sheffield Wednesday on Friday. In both boxes, they remain wholly deficient and soft, even.

Industry observers note that reflecting on events on the night at Bradford, Gale didn't shy away from that damning word. Soft.

"I think if you watched that, I don't think you can dispute that”, the former Gillingham man told The Yorkshire Post.

"It hurts to admit (that), I'm a centre-half and pride myself on defending.

"Bradford were a team of men who defended their box and blocked and headed everything and made sure no-one had an opportunity and ultimately we gave up really poor goals.

"We're coming up to the Christmas period and games are coming thick and fast with plenty of points to play for. Seasons can be won and lost.

According to recent reports, "You can really turn your season around or it can go the other way. We've got to be around each other, address what we have to and it probably means a lot of home truths with each other and we've probably got to all look at ourselves.

Recent findings suggest that "There were some home truths in there at full-time (at Bradford). It was necessary and needed.

"Ultimately, the management team could do nothing to affect the goals. The goals were poor and had nothing to do with tactics, shape or formations.

In a recent development, "There were three long balls we didn't deal with. And we haven't put the finishing touch in their box. That's the difference.”.

Gale was culpable for the first goal from ex-Reds striker Stephen Humphrys when he made a hash of coping with a goal-kick from Bantams keeper Jon McCracken. It was compounded by meek defending from Arley Kay, who was shrugged off too easily by the goalscorer.

How Gale, 22 - in his first season in League One - and Kay, who turns 19 in February, would benefit from having a hardened defensive lieutenant alongside them who knows the level to learn from.

Gale added: "It was poor from me for the first goal and it sets the tone.

"This was a perfect example of a game being won in both boxes.

It has been revealed that "By a country mile, we were the best side between both boxes. But it's irrelevant, they defended their box and were savvy with blocks, pushes, nudges and not letting you have anything.

In a recent development, "In our box, they were also savvy with the same thing and they got opportunities from it. That was the story.

According to recent reports, "After the Sheffield Wednesday game, we talked about set-pieces and how we needed to defend them better and we did that. We still conceded three poor goals which were very similar - probably a cut and paste of each other. It's not one simple solution unfortunately.

"All we can do is put ourselves first and come together as a team because it has to get better.".

Between now and the close of play on January 1, Barnsley, who have taken a pitiful two points from the last available 33 - face several sides in the bottom half of the table, starting with AFC Wimbledon on Saturday.

Their points haul could well decide whether they have a realistic chance of survival before addressing things in a January window they simply cannot afford to get wrong.

Recent findings suggest that in the circumstances, Barnsley's support was admirable and stoic at Valley Parade. Their patience did snap at the end when a late penalty from Jake Beesley made it 3-0, but it was understandable.

"They are within their rights to be unhappy. Barnsley is a big football club with a big history and we're bottom of League One," Gale noted.

"I'd be negative too if I was a fan - I'm a football fan myself - and paying my hard-earned money and travelling up and down the country to watch my team not win in 11 games, I'd have something to say as well.

"We've just got to take it and wear it. They are the reasons we are playing for this football club. Going into Saturday, we've got to block out the noise and give them something to cheer about.".

Leeds transfer news: Will Lankshear January hopes shot down by 44-goal striker

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 25 Nov 2026 11:33.
  • Former Leeds United striker Brian Deane, speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, has played down the Whites' chances of signing Will Lankshear in the January transfer window.
  • The former Tottenham Hotspur youngster has taken the Championship by storm since moving to the Riverside Stadium in the summer, scoring 14 goals in 15 second-tier appearances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 25 Nov 2026 11:33.

Former Leeds United striker Brian Deane, speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, has played down the Whites' chances of signing Will Lankshear in the January transfer window.

The former Tottenham Hotspur youngster has taken the Championship by storm since moving to the Riverside Stadium in the summer, scoring 14 goals in 15 second-tier appearances.

Lankshear netted the winner as Middlesbrough beat Swansea City 2-1 on Tuesday night, a result that saw Kim Hellberg's men move one point clear of Wolverhampton Wanderers at the top of the Championship table.

The 21-year-old unsurprisingly sits top of the Championship top scorers charts, three clear of closest challenger Andri Gudjohnsen of Blackburn Rovers in the race for the Golden Boot.

Lankshear's form has inevitably led to speculation surrounding a swift return to the Premier League, with multiple clubs believed to be interested in securing his services, including Leeds.

Former club Tottenham, Arsenal, Brighton & Hove Albion and Newcastle United have also been credited with an interest, although Middlesbrough's £70m asking price could deter suitors.

Now, former Leeds forward Deane - who scored 44 goals in 199 matches for the Whites - has expressed his view that Lankshear should remain at the Riverside Stadium over the winter.

“This is his breakout season, and he is at a good club," Deane told Sports Mole. "Middlesbrough look on course to challenge for promotion, so hopefully he gets there with them.

“He will be ambitious and attract attention from clubs such as Leeds, Brighton and Newcastle. He would be a good addition to a squad. But for his own development, I think he is in a good place at Middlesbrough.”.

Lankshear made just six senior appearances for Tottenham before being sold in a £9.8m deal over the summer, and the striker's contract with Middlesbrough does not expire until 2031.

A young striker scoring for fun in the Championship will always attract glances from top-tier clubs, but Lankshear may struggle to force his way into Daniel Farke's first XI right now.

First-choice pairing Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor boast a respectable nine Premier League goals between them in 2026-27, and as long as both are fit, they will spearhead Farke's 3-5-2 system.

Calvert-Lewin is now in the final 24 months of his contract at Elland Road, but the England international is understood to be close to signing a upcoming Leeds deal.

Lukas Nmecha also provides a steady backup option, although he is due to become a free agent in 2027 and may seek a move away in January if his game-time situation does not improve.

However, Nmecha's proposed exit would then open the door for summer signing Jean-Matteo Bahoya to earn more opportunities, so a winter move for Lankshear would make little sense for all involved.

Brian Deane was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of BetWright.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a sport obsessed with the next major thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 05:00 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EST, 25 November 2026.

In a sport obsessed with the next major thing, there is more attention than ever being paid to teenage prodigies who appear destined for the very top.

The latest player to have fans raving is former Manchester United academy star JJ Gabriel, 16, who joined the club aged nine but stunned those at Old Trafford by asking to leave. He is now closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

The acrimonious nature of the teenager's departure has left Gabriel vulnerable to a spectacular fall from grace, particularly after his team released montages showing him joining an agency and saying goodbye to United.

The spotlight is well and truly burning on Gabriel, and he would do well to learn the lessons of other youngsters who were tipped for greatness but ultimately crashed and burned.

It has been revealed that of course, injuries, personal problems and media pressure can all weigh heavily on a young player's prospects. There are countless pitfalls that mean tomorrow's stars often burn out before they have had the chance to shine.

Here, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over some of the most famous wonderkids who never managed to live up to their potential.

Wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 16, confirmed his exit from Manchester United on Tuesday night.

In 2004, Freddy Adu was viewed as the future of American football. Dubbed 'The Next Pele', the Ghanaian-born talent was the youngest professional athlete in major American sports when he signed his first contract at just 14.

It has been revealed that the hype was extraordinary. He became MLS's highest-paid player, secured a lucrative Nike contract and appeared in an advert alongside Pele himself.

But things never quite worked out for the attacking midfielder. After three years at DC United and Real Salt Lake, he made the much-anticipated move to Europe, joining Benfica for £1million in 2007. It was largely downhill from there.

After making just 11 appearances in three years in Portugal, he moved to Monaco before embarking on a series of unsuccessful and increasingly disappointing loan spells in Portugal, Turkey and Greece. He eventually ended up at Brazilian club Bahia in 2013.

Industry observers note that from that point, Adu floated around clubs in Brazil, Serbia, Finland, the US and Sweden. He last played competitive fooball for Swedish third-tier side Osterlen in 2021, aged 32. He remains one of football's biggest 'what if' stories.

Freddy Adu was dubbed 'The Next Pele' but he never fulfilled anywhere near his potential.

Once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as 'the best player I have ever seen at his age', Ravel Morrison is a particularly unfortunate case of an English prospect failing to make the most of an extraordinarily promising career.

As a fresh-faced 17-year-old, he arrived at Carrington with the talent and ability to become one of the world's best players.

He had all the attributes of a world-class attacking midfielder and appeared mature beyond his years on the pitch. Off it, however, was a different story.

In early 2011, barely a year after signing his first professional contract with Manchester United, he was charged with witness intimidation in connection with a domestic violence case.

Since then, although he has never served time in prison, Morrison has faced several further charges, including assault, harassment and fraud. His repeated off-field troubles ultimately derailed a career that had once promised so much.

Industry observers note that morrison has gone on to represent 15 clubs during a career spanning 16 years, failing to fulfil the promise that once enchanted Ferguson. He is at the moment plying his trade in the second tier of UAE football.

Ravel Morrison was one of the most talented players to come through Man United's academy.

It has been revealed that the first Brazilian on this list is former Manchester City forward Robinho. Having come through the Santos academy – a production line that has also delivered the likes of Pele and Neymar – he was expected to become the next superstar to emerge from the club's illustrious ranks.

Industry observers note that however, a series of setbacks meant he never quite fulfilled that early promise. Robinho followed in the footsteps of Brazilian stars such as Adriano, Dani Alves and Kaka by moving to Europe at a young age, joining Real Madrid in 2005.

He enjoyed a promising start to his career, making more than 100 appearances for Los Blancos and winning two league titles before turning 24.

But his move to Manchester City in 2008 failed to take his career to the next level. In fact, things began to unravel.

Recent findings suggest that the Brazilian did not get off to the best of starts. Upon arriving in Manchester, he revealed that 'Chelsea had made a great proposal, and I accepted'.

What followed were two underwhelming years at the Etihad, where he scored 16 goals in 53 appearances and spent much of his second season in England sidelined by injury.

Robinho subsequently joined AC Milan before spells with a number of Turkish clubs and a return to Brazil. He never again reached the heights of his early career.

The Brazilian is right now imprisoned after being found guilty of sexual assault in connection with an incident at a Milan nightclub in 2013. He began serving his nine-year sentence in 2024.

Former Man City star Robinho never quite fulfilled the early promise he had back in Brazil.

Another case reminiscent of Adu's: a young superstar who was seemingly rated too highly before we ever really got to see him play.

Mastour caught the eye of Italian giants AC Milan after gaining notoriety on YouTube. His video, uploaded in 2012 and titled 'The Best 14-year-old in the World', showcased the Moroccan's impressive array of skills and tricks, making him one of football's first viral sensations.

Recent findings suggest that the hype surrounding Mastour was staggering, with the youngster securing a lucrative endorsement deal with Nike. Before long, he was posing alongside Neymar in a photoshoot.

In a recent development, but the success never materialised for the tricky forward. During four years on AC Milan's books, he failed to make a single first-team appearance and managed just six outings during loan spells at Malaga and Dutch side PEC Zwolle.

Industry observers note that the Moroccan, now 28, plays in the fourth tier of Italian football. Quite how such a highly rated prospect failed to fulfil his potential remains a mystery.

Hachim Mastour dazzled as a teenager on the internet but ended up a long way from the top.

From one player who never showed his quality to one who only a decade ago was the recipient of the coveted Golden Boy award for the best under-21 player in Europe.

Renato Sanches was an absolute phenomenon, the box-to-box midfielder burst onto the scene in the 2015-16 season at Benfica – earning himself a place on the plane to France with Portugal for the 2016 Euros where he played a pivotal role in his nation's triumph.

Those performances saw a host of European giants fight it out to land the then-18-year-old, with Bayern Munich emerging triumphant – landing the midfielder in a deal rising to £63million.

However, Sanches failed to hit his stride in Germany and he was soon shipped out on loan to Swansea – where he was best remembered for passing the ball to an advertising hoarding.

It has been revealed that he enjoyed a small resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, paving the way for a move to PSG. But once again, the big transfer failed to work out, and he now finds himself with Greek side Panathinaikos.

He enjoyed a resurgence at Lille, winning Ligue 1 and the French Super Cup, which paved the way for a move to Paris Saint-Germain.

But once again, a significant-money move failed to work out, and he now finds himself at Greek side Panathinaikos.

Renato Sanches (pictured at Roma in 2024) now plies his trade in Greece with Panathinaikos.

Alexandre Pato had the world at his feet, but his body ultimately failed to deliver on the extraordinary talent he possessed.

The Brazilian was an electric centre-forward who lit up European football. His goal against Barcelona in the Champions League, scored after just 24 seconds at the age of 22, was a perfect illustration of his frightening ability.

His pace, agility and clinical finishing saw him touted as a future world-beater, while he was named Golden Boy.

Alexandre Pato is another wonderkid who saw their career hampered by a string of injuries.

Yet persistent injury problems made it almost impossible for Pato to fulfil his early promise.

In a recent development, the Brazilian struggled with ankle, Achilles and muscle problems throughout his career. As the injuries mounted, his outstanding physical attributes began to wane, rendering the qualities that had once terrified defenders increasingly ineffective.

It has been revealed that after six years at AC Milan, Pato returned to Brazil to join Corinthians. He spent two years with the club before embarking on short spells at Chelsea and Villarreal, neither of which yielded lasting success.

Rounding off this list is another English talent who once looked destined for the very top but has since seen his career take a downward turn.

Back in 2019, there were few hotter prospects in world football than Jadon Sancho. The then 19-year-old had made the brave decision two years earlier to leave England, having spent several impressive years in Manchester City's academy, and join Bundesliga giants Borussia Dortmund.

Sources indicate that it seemed a bizarre move at the time, but the switch proved to be a stroke of genius. Sancho was handed regular first-team football and flourished, registering 40 goals and 54 assists in just 118 Bundesliga appearances. He also collected a DFB-Pokal winner's medal.

By 2021, the boy from Kennington had the world at his feet, with a host of suitors willing to break the bank to secure his services.

Jadon Sancho once had the world at his feet but has found himself stuck in a downward spiral.

According to recent reports, after a summer-long transfer saga, Sancho eventually joined Manchester United for an eye-watering £73million, reportedly earning £350,000 per week. It proved to be a nightmare move for both parties.

The Englishman had to wait until late November to score his first United goal in his debut season and never consistently rediscovered his best form.

In January 2024, he returned to Germany and enjoyed a revival, helping guide Dortmund to the Champions League final, where they lost to Real Madrid at Wembley.

Two unsuccessful loan spells at Chelsea and Aston Villa followed before Sancho left United as a free agent last summer. He remains without a club at the age of 26, just five years after his mega-money move.

For all the promising youngsters who struggle to live up to the hype, there are also teen sensations who navigate the pitfalls of professional football to achieve great things.

Kylian Mbappe helped Monaco win their first Ligue 1 title for 17 years having broken into the team as a 16-year-old. His progress since then has been remarkable and he remains one of the world's very best at Real Madrid.

His team-mate Vinicius Jr signed for Real Madrid to much fanfare as an 18-year-old and has lived up to it all for both club and country.

While you could argue that Neymar could have achieved more, he has still enjoyed a stellar career across the globe and become the highest-scoring Brazilian player in history for the national side after signing for Barcelona, as one of the most talked-about starlets.

Wayne Rooney broke through for Everton at 16 and went on to have a brilliant career.

When you look closer to home, Wayne Rooney and Michael Owen broke through as exciting 16-year-olds and both reached the very highest level.

Paolo Maldini made his AC Milan debut at 16 and became one of the all-time great centre-backs and Cesc Fabregas developed into a world class midfielder after getting selected at the same age for Arsenal.

Going back further, Diego Maradona was playing senior football at 15, as did Ronaldo Nazario, while Lionel Messi embarked on his extraordinary career at 16.

JJ Gabriel and his management will be hoping that when all is stated and done - his name is associated with this category and avoid joining the starlets who never quite made it.

How Sheffield United's 'dinosaur' changed tactics to turn game against Southampton

💡 Key Takeaways

  • For half an hour the Blades were outclassed by a Saints side who looked Premier League-ready.
  • Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A game which began like a demonstration of how short the Blades were of the Championship elite ended with them proving they have what it takes to mix it with them.

For half an hour the Blades were outclassed by a Saints side who looked Premier League-ready. The Blades had only just over 20 per cent of the ball, which for them in a Championship home game is extremely rare.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

When Hamza Choudhury gave it away and failed to stop Lewis Dobbin curling the ball in, it was no less than the Saints deserved.

But from that unpromising start, the hosts turned it around. The second half was pretty much all them, so when Daniel Peretz saved brilliantly from Tahith Chong in the 83rd minute, you wondered if it was going to be one of those nights.

But the drama was just beginning. Jordan Ayew, who had shown what mood he was in with a nutmeg in the middle of the pitch, produced another in the 90th minute as he beat two men along the byline and teed up Sydie Peck to equalise. It still could have all been for nothing had Blades goalkeeper Michael Cooper not made a crucial save one-on-one with Samuel Edozie in the third added minute.

“The concentration of Michael was absolutely outstanding and the save was great,” commented Wilder.

“It would have been incredibly cruel if we'd have not got a result.

"There would (still) have been a certain amount of pride - not enjoyment because when you play as well as that, you have to get something.

"But I think I'd have put my head on the pillow and I would have gone, whatever the result, I don't think they've been dealt with like we've dealt with them in the second half.".

As for the other bit, Tonda Eckert played the Blades the compliment of moving the player who normally operates in the hole in front of James Ward-Prowse and Flynn Downes to sit between them and the back four.

Industry observers note that "They've got really technical players, and we didn't get to grips with their shape," admitted Wilder. "They had control of the game, they had seven touches in our box in the first half.

"So the old man, the dinosaur, had to get to grips with their press, our press, which we did after half an hour.

Industry observers note that "We just wanted the two wide players to jump a little bit earlier and we needed to get around their six (holding midfielder) because the six was dominating and dictating the game. So we stuck somebody a little bit higher, got around their six and had a little bit of a change at the back, just slid over and got more pressure on the ball. In the second half we've had 31 touches in the box, 16 shots, 71 per cent possession.

Recent findings suggest that "We made really good footballers resort to just clearing the lines for the last 20, 25 minutes. Sometimes, when you look back on draws, it's bigger than just the draw, with the performance against a side of the quality that we played against.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most uplifting facets of Martin Drury's full-time tenure has been the transformation so far in 2026-27.

A good barometer of their improvement arrives in tonight's Yorkshire derby at Doncaster Rovers - on an evening when three points would see the Terriers move level on points with leaders Stockport County.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

A poor night at the South Yorkshire venue in February saw Town lose 1-0 in a toothless and tepid showing which received jeers from travelling fans at half-time and the final whistle.

Industry observers note that it was one a number of bad days on the road. Others were played out at Oakwell, Valley Parade and further afield at Adams Park and Home Park.

There were plenty more too, especially in the second half of the season when the entertainment value was lamentably low.

In the away table in 25-26, Huddersfield were ranked a below-par 13th, with 25 points from 23 games. Refreshingly, the picture is changing, not just in terms of points ratio, but goals and chance creation.

According to recent reports, town have averaged two points a game on the road so far, with 14 points from their seven matches. It's presently the second best record in the division, factoring in goal difference.

Recent findings suggest that drury observed: "There was some criticism of the away form last season. Obviously, I came in February. Between February and the end of the season, the away form wasn't brilliant.

"Prior to that, for the seven months before that, there weren't enough points picked up on the road. And if you want to be successful, you need to do that.

"So that was certainly an area that we addressed in the summer. And we did some things around that with the players, both on and off the grass, around certain scenarios and places that you're going to go to and how we might play when we're home and away. I think the players have been brilliant.

"I think we're fourth or third best in the league, maybe, for away form at the current time.

"We're going to lose some games away. That's going to happen. But I have to say, the things that we wanted to try and learn from last season and get better at, the players have done really, really well with that.

"And we've gone to some tough places so far with different types of challenges that we've enjoyed and embraced.".

Recent findings suggest that town face a Rovers side who don't usually mind derbies. They excelled, certainly in the first half, of the home game with Sheffield Wednesday last month and indicated character to come from behind to secure a hard-earned stoppage-time point at Bradford City on Saturday.

The latter derby marked the first-team return of ex-Terriers defender Matty Pearson after almost two-and-a-half months out with injury.

Pearson came through the weekend draw, while Jamie Sterry, James Husband and Tommi O’Reilly are all in contention for tonight's game.

Sources indicate that eager to make up for lost time, Pearson commented: "It's one of those things, you feel helpless when you're injured. It's been a tough few months but I'm well past that now.

"It's how you handle things and react. I think everyone's career has ups and downs and it's how you bounce back and how you react to them situations.".

Pearson unquestionably had a mixed time during his four seasons at Huddersfield.

In a recent development, the Keighley-born player continued: "It was a big change really. We had an unbelievable first season (2021-22) and got into the play-offs and final (against Nottingham Forest at Wembley).

"And then it was 'sliding doors'. I don't know the full ins and outs but we struggled for the following two or three seasons after that. We went from playoffs to relegation battles every season.

"It's hard to say exactly what went on, it's one of those where it's been taken over now and they look like they're having a good season so far.".

While Town have incentives this evening, so do Rovers; victory would see them move out of the relegation zone and jump up three places to 18th.

Drury added: "They obviously scored late on Saturday, which gives them a little bit of a boost when they get a goal to draw the game.

"I'm sure they've wanted to pick up more points than they have done this season, but I think they're a team with energy and players that want to get on the ball and play and take the ball under pressure.

"They're a team that have scored a lot of goals from set-pieces and scored goals from transition, so they can attack fast.

Recent findings suggest that "But for all the stats, there's also a lot of things where we feel we can impose ourselves and really hurt them. We're in a good place.".

Sources indicate that star Town winger Derensili Sanches Fernandes is available for tonight's game, despite coming off with a slight foot issue/cramp on Saturday's loss to Leicester City. David Kasumu and Samson Tovide are sidelined.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ex-England striker Carlton Cole has slammed Manchester United’s recruitment under INEOS and claims it was ‘criminal’ the club didn’t explore a move for Danny Welbeck in the summer.

There had been a sense of optimism amongst United’s fanbase heading into the season after Michael Carrick picked up the pieces from Ruben Amorim’s turbulent reign to lead the club to a third-place finish last term.

But the Red Devils once again find themselves in a state of disarray after a wretched start to the 2026/27 campaign, which ultimately cost Carrick his job earlier this month.

With genuine fears growing that United could become embroiled in a relegation scrap, Mauricio Pochettino has been tasked with steadying the ship and steering a dispirited squad away from the bottom of the Premier League table.

The Argentine’s tenure got off to a nightmare start at the weekend, though, as his side were put to the sword at the hands of arch-rivals Liverpool in a thumping 4-0 defeat at Anfield.

Sunday’s result ensured United remain firmly in the drop zone after 11 matches, only one point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace with the worst defensive record of any team in Europe’s top five leagues.

If Pochettino was expecting to be supported with significant financial backing in his efforts to turn United’s fortunes around this winter, he will likely be disappointed.

After all, Reports this week suggest the 54-year-old will have a budget of ‘well under £50million’ to work with when the January transfer window opens for business.

According to recent reports, asked what Pochettino must address with his meagre funds while tackling United’s woes on The Dressing Room Podcast, Cole replied: ‘The spine. They haven’t got a striker, a worthy striker.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Midfield, I think they’re alright there for now because they’ve got Carlos Baleba and I think he’s a fantastic player by the way, they’ve got Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes… I think they’re alright in that position.

Sources indicate that ‘I know the boy from Chelsea, Andrey Santos, he’s there, but I know he’s not tuned in yet because it’s high pressure right now and he’s a little bit off it. They’ve got Youri Tielemans as well. Then you’ve got the centre-backs…’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to Cole, United missed a trick when they gave Chelsea a free run at signing Welbeck from Brighton in the summer.

‘I think it’s criminal they didn’t sign Welbeck,’ he added.

‘I think he’s wasted at Chelsea at the moment, they should have signed Welbeck. He’d have done alright!’.

Eyebrows were raised when Pochettino named his team to face Liverpool on Sunday, with Matthijs de Ligt thrown in for his first Premier League start of the campaign.

There were signs of rustiness in De Ligt’s game from minute one and it was the Dutchman’s calamitous defending that led to Dominik Szoboszlai’s breakthrough – and Leny Yoro’s sending off – after only ten minutes.

‘I thought that was him [Pochettino] protesting already,’ Cole remarked of De Ligt’s surprise selection.

‘I think it was on the first or second day that he was in, he was already saying he wanted more control in the transfer market. I thought you negotiated that in your deal!

‘He’s chosen the right time to do it [make a protest], in a game like that.

Recent findings suggest that ‘This was a free hit for him and yes, he needs defenders. But I’ve noted it before, INEOS have gone with signing forward first and then the next window they get a midfielder… who does that? So that’s what has happened.’.

Cole went a step further on Pochettino’s decision to field De Ligt, adding: ‘I think it’s bang out of order, he’s been stitched up.

‘He’s obviously not fit, he can’t read it. When you’ve been out so long, you get your bearings wrong, you don’t know where you are on the pitch. It happens, right? So I give him grace for that.

According to recent reports, ‘The problem is that Yoro is not experienced. So if you’re going to bring in De Ligt, you’ve got to bring another experienced defender in with him.

‘If De Ligt is going to be there and Harry Maguire is there then it’s alright and if Maguire makes that mistake that Yoro made, I get it.

Industry observers note that ‘But Yoro is still young, he’s still learning the game. They’re both, to some extent, inexperienced at this moment in time so it’s the blind leading the blind.’.

United will look to stop the rot when they switch their focus to Champions League matters away to Sporting on Wednesday evening.

Three days later, Pochettino’s men return to Premier League action at home to Brentford.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 12:36.

Such is Unai Emery's status at Aston Villa that few would be surprised if the redeveloped North Stand, when completed in 2027, is named after the Spaniard.

Taking Villa from relegation candidates in 2022-23 to two Champions League qualifications and a Europa League trophy by the conclusion of 2025-26 arguably deserves that level of recognition.

However, despite the expectation that a contract extension past 2029 will be penned in the near future, it will not necessarily strengthen Emery's, or the club's, position in the long term.

It has been revealed that tuesday's 1-0 defeat at Galatasaray extended Villa's recent winless streak across all competitions to six matches. They have failed to score in four of those games, and given up leads on three occasions.

Sources indicate that emery is no stranger to an extended blip in form. At the start of both 2025-26 and 2026-27, Villa were off the pace. It is to Emery's credit that Villa became brief Premier League title contenders in a matter of months and still finished in fourth position in last season's standings.

Nevertheless, Villa are now enduring their second extended winless period of the season, raising the question of whether the West Midlands outfit are experiencing a blip or a gradual decline under their most successful manager for nearly 45 years?

With 116 wins from 215 matches, silverware, and delivering moments and experiences that will last a lifetime, Emery is etched into the Villa history books as a God.

In a recent development, at the same time, this is now a manager of a team that has only recorded 11 wins from his last 27 games in all competitions, as well as losing on 10 occasions. Just seven wins have come from 19 fixtures in 2026-27.

When Villa defeated Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United and Manchester City in relatively quick succession with performances that mixed grit, shrewdness and attacking vigour, the conclusion was that Emery's latest-looked team had flicked a switch.

It has been revealed that however, Villa have regressed as quickly as they had seemingly improved. When you take into account that Villa had one win in seven between February 1 and March 4, and lost three in a row between April 25 and May 3, this is now the fourth "blip" in less than nine months.

According to recent reports, some of the aforementioned statistics will be comparable with managers at similarly-sized clubs in the Premier League and Europe, yet that usually leads to scrutiny over the job that has been conducted over a specific period. Not talk of a contract until 2030 and beyond being signed.

By modern-day standards, Emery is in the unique position of having high control over which players are signed and sold. He essentially has the keys to the footballing side of the club and Villa's fate on the pitch is solely in his hands.

Yet, a 12-time trophy-winning manager of a team that has only earned fewer Premier League points than Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool across a four-year period is frequently telling the media, or anyone who will listen, that Villa should not be competing in the top six, nor for the top-eight positions in the league phase of the Champions League.

Is this an example of Emery trying to reinforce the perception that Villa are underdogs to the so-called Premier League 'major six' because of what is, admittedly, a scandalous PSR scenario, or is it a pre-orchestrated approach to defend his position whenever results do not go Villa's way?

Staying on the subject of things being pre-orchestrated, not enough scrutiny is coming over Villa's and Emery's use of Liverpool's Harvey Elliott and Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho.

Sources indicate that since the summer of 2025, Villa have included £35m and, allegedly, £43m fees with those clubs to sign the players in question should they achieve a specific appearance threshold. Between them, they have made three starts and 13 substitute outings when spending the majority of the time available for selection.

Industry observers note that on Tuesday night, Emery omitted Garnacho - who has accumulated fewer than 100 minutes across seven substitute appearances - from the squad for the Galatasaray match, despite naming one fewer substitute than was permitted. Afterwards, he delivered a frank response over the Argentine's chances of earning future game time.

If Villa do not want to pay vast amounts of money for players, they do not have to. However, are Villa not harming their chances of signing players through similar deals in the future? Why should clubs trust such deals to go through if Emery is choosing not to select such players or is being told not to?

Everything points to Garnacho becoming Elliott 2:0 and the situation deserves some clarity. If an honest assessment cannot be delivered to fans and the media, Emery leaves himself open to persistent questioning and criticism, and it will be warranted.

Of course, the evolving Garnacho saga can change for the better. Excluding Villa's game against Chelsea in December, the winger has seven more chances to feature in 2026.

Industry observers note that there can be a rapid upturn in fortunes, too. Villa face Ipswich Town, Everton and Crystal Palace in the Premier League before they welcome Paris Saint-Germain to Villa Park in the Champions League.

However, when Emery is storming down tunnels before the full-time whistle, throwing tantrums in the media and getting increasingly frustrated on the touchline as his team look slow, devoid of ideas and can make 700 passes in a game and not score against a team such as Sunderland, it can be argued that Villa need a change of direction rather than remaining on their current path.

According to recent reports, villa have a deep squad with talent that can earn them success in the future, yet they have too many under-performers or players who may simply be tired even at this stage of the season. Whether that is down to Emery, or too much emphasis being placed on players needing to adapt to the "Emery way" before they earn regular starts, it is open to debate.

Regardless, Villa are presently on a downward trajectory under his leadership, and Emery has questions to answer if he is to remain untouchable at a club that want to hand him a contract extension when they could enter December with just three Premier League wins in 2026-27.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Monza star Gustavo Varela has distanced himself from speculation that he could be set for a January transfer move and insists he is ‘paying no attention’ to incessant rumours linking him with Arsenal, Barcelona and Napoli.

Varela, 21, was deemed surplus to requirements at Benfica and completed a switch to newly promoted Italian outfit Monza for a fee of just €2million (£1.7m) – plus performance-related bonuses – in the summer.

It has proven a tough start to the season for Monza on their return to Serie A, with the club picking up just three wins and languishing down in 14th place in the table.

Varela has proven a shining light up front, though, scoring 11 goals in his opening 11 top-flight appearances, and the striker’s barnstorming form in Lombardy has begun to attract the attentions of European football’s elite.

According to recent reports emanating out of Varela’s native Portugal, Barca, Napoli and Arsenal are all actively pursuing a deal for the forward on the back of his goalscoring exploits in the first three months of the campaign.

Premier League champions Arsenal are noted to be among a host of Premier League clubs that have ‘expressed an interest’ in Varela and were ‘one of the first to enquire’ about the player’s potential availability.

It’s understood the Gunners are in the market for an attacker of Varela’s profile, with Viktor Gyokeres struggling to live up to expectations following his £64m arrival from Sporting last year.

On Monday night, Varela ensured he remained in the headlines with a terrific brace in Monza’s 3-0 victory over Fiorentina – in doing so, becoming only the third player in the last 50 years to reach the double figures in their first 11 Serie A games.

‘I can’t believe what I’m doing. I go home, close my eyes and I can’t believe it. Football is made of moments,’ Varela told DAZN Italy following Monza’s win.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

On his brilliant flicked effort to complete his double, Varela added: ‘It was pure instinct, it’s not something I practice.

‘A very beautiful cross came in, I was close to the goal and I decided to try my luck. If you don’t try, you can’t do it, and it happened.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Varela was then asked for his reaction the rumoured interest he was receiving from some of Europe’s most high-profile teams, to which he responded: ‘I continue to thank Monza for allowing me to be here. It has all been incredible.

‘I feel lucky to be part of this reality and I only hope to continue on this path.

Sources indicate that ‘I pay no attention to the news. I only focus on what I have to do on the field. It’s normal, it’s part of football.

‘I’m going through a great moment but a less good moment may arise tomorrow.

Trust us, you're going to want to watch this OUTRAGEOUS finish from Gustavo Varela 😮‍💨🔥#MonzaFiorentina #UNROSSOALLAVIOLENZA pic.twitter.com/Z2RvJFul6X.

‘That’s why I try to simply enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.

‘Sometimes they speak well of me and sometimes they speak badly, but this is the world of football and I only think about what I have to do on the field.’.

Monza are believed to have slapped an asking price on Varela in the region of €40-50m (£33-42m).

Though they did not insert a buy-back clause in their deal with Monza for Varela, Benfica will be entitled to 20 per cent of any future transfer fee for the sought-after youngster.

The Primeira Liga club also have the right of first refusal should a bidding war break out for the Portugal Under-21 international, who was named the Serie A Rising Star of the Month for October.

Varela’s current contract with Monza runs through to June 2030.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 12:37.
  • Venezia head into their matchday 13 encounter with in-form Bologna seeking a third league victory in four matches at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo.
  • The Europe-chasing visitors sit 11 places above the Veneto-based club in the Serie A table but will be wary of the Winged Lions' recent improvement in front of their supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 12:37.

Venezia head into their matchday 13 encounter with in-form Bologna seeking a third league victory in four matches at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo.

The Europe-chasing visitors sit 11 places above the Veneto-based club in the Serie A table but will be wary of the Winged Lions' recent improvement in front of their supporters.

On the surface, Venezia's decision to replace Giovanni Stroppa with Davide Nicola has made little difference to their results, with the Lagunari sitting bottom of the league.

However, a closer look suggests that the home supporters can expect a battling performance when Bologna travel to Venice on Friday.

Still the only Serie A side yet to draw this term, the promoted outfit have suffered 10 defeats in 12 matches, including four since Nicola's appointment in October.

Nonetheless, all six of their points have come from their last three matches at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo, where they have beaten Napoli (1-0) and Udinese (2-1) either side of a 2-0 defeat to Inter Milan.

That loss to the defending champions came courtesy of own goals from Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal in the final 10 minutes, with the bottom-placed side attempting 12 shots to Inter's 16 and creating two clear-cut chances to the Nerazzurri's three.

Although three matches represent a small sample, those recent performances in Venice suggest that the Lagunari are slowly turning the tide at home, giving Bologna reason for caution ahead of Friday's trip.

Raffaele Palladino's Rossoblu know all about upturns in form, having experienced their own resurgence since Domenico Tedesco was dismissed in mid-September following a winless start to the campaign.

A 1-0 defeat to Napoli at the Maradona proved the final straw for the hierarchy in Bologna, with Palladino inheriting a Felsinei side that had collected just one point from an available 12 across four matches.

Sitting 16th at the time and outside the bottom three only on goal difference, the Rossoblu have since collected 17 points from a possible 24 under Palladino to climb to ninth on 18 points, just three behind sixth-placed Juventus.

Only Lazio (22), AC Milan (19) and Roma (18) have earned more points during that period, underlining Bologna's resurgence since Tedesco's departure as they target a sixth victory in nine league matches.

The travelling supporters will therefore back their in-form side to overcome Nicola's men, although the result may be less straightforward than some anticipate given the Lagunari's steady improvement on home turf.

Toma Basic (muscle), Thierry Correia (thigh), Pasquale Mazzocchi (muscle), Andrea Adorante (hernia), Marin Sverko (hip) and Bartol Franjic (shoulder) are all considered unlikely to feature in gameweek 13.

No player has scored more than twice for the division's lowest scorers, with Akor Adams and Antoine Hainaut netting two apiece to account for half of the Winged Lions' eight league goals.

While Bologna have no individual producing spectacular numbers, they boast a broader spread of match-winners, with Federico Bernardeschi, Samuel Mbangula, Riccardo Orsolini and Tommaso Pobega all scoring twice.

Although Juan Miranda, Nicolo Cambiaghi and Jens Odgaard have yet to score, their respective returns of five, three and two assists underline their importance to the Rossoblu.

However, Bologna must manage without Miranda, who is sidelined alongside Jay Enem (Achilles), Oussama El Azzouzi (thigh) and Emil Holm (thigh).

Venezia possible starting lineup:.

Stankovic; Halhal, Moreno, Juan Jesus; Hainaut, Kike Perez, Sohm, Busio, Haps; Lauberbach, Adams.

Bologna possible starting lineup:.

Skorupski; Darmian, Casale, Theate; Zortea, Ferguson, Pobega, Cambiaghi; Bernardeschi, Orsolini; Odgaard.

Venezia's victories over Napoli and Udinese suggest that their lowly position does not tell the whole story, particularly after they made Inter work for their points in Venice.

However, Bologna's 17-point return from eight matches under Palladino reflects a more sustained improvement, and the visitors should have enough attacking variety to edge Friday's encounter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hallam FC, one of the grand old names of football, have temporarily ceased playing the game they helped forge amid dire financial circumstances and an explosive war of words between newly introduced and old owners.

The Sheffield club, founded in 1860 and whose ground at Sandygate is the oldest in the world, have withdrawn from the Northern Premier League East with immediate effect.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

In a statement released on Thursday, Hallam officials say the club’s financial position is “perilous” and that had they continued playing, they would have a deficit of £69,000 by the end of the year.

Recent findings suggest that new officials only came to the club in October when Andy Emsley was voted in as chairman. The new officials allege that Hallam FC owed a £13,500 VAT bill for the period from July to October, a debt they have now set out a timeline with PAYE to repay.

The claims have been rejected by former club chairman Richard Pillinger in a statement on behalf of the previous board on X, in which he accuses the fresh hierarchy of “seriously misleading and libellous allegations”.

It has been revealed that in the initial club statement, Hallam officials wrote: “Contrary to what the former club officers led you to believe at the AGM, the financial position of the club is perilous. Our projections show that without radical action the club is heading for a deficit of at least £69k at the year end and the cashflow position indicates that we could well run out of money in December.

“In this very challenging situation, club officers discussed the options available to us, we very reluctantly agreed that withdrawal from the NPL East for the 26/27 season was the most appropriate action to take in the circumstances.

Sources indicate that “In our view it would be dishonest for the club to continue to try to play fixtures in the NPL East when we know how difficult the financial position is. There is a high risk we would be asking players to commit to games and staff to attend to work when we know that there is a significant risk that we may not be able to pay them, similarly with suppliers.

“That would be a totally unacceptable situation.

“In making this agonising decision we are trying to do the right thing by the club, the players, our suppliers and the community.”.

It has been revealed that former chairman Mr Pillinger replied with his own statement which read: “The previous board of Hallam FC has seen the statement released by the present incumbents this morning. Our immediate response is as follows:.

“1. We are stunned and horrified that the club has pulled out of league competition. This unprecedented and disastrous move will never be forgotten and is a permanent scar the club will have to bear.

“2. We entirely reject the seriously misleading and we believe libellous allegations made today. We are seeking urgent legal advice accordingly.

According to recent reports, “3. We will therefore provide a comprehensive response in due course but in the meantime urge the present incumbents to withdraw this defamatory statement. Failure to withdraw and apologise immediately will leave us with no choice other than to explore every possible action available to us at this time.”.

The upcoming regime hope to restore Hallam FC back into the pyramid next season.

Industry observers note that the club statement added: “Despite the painful decision to withdraw from the NPL East, Hallam Football Club still exists. “We will take the next few months to sort out the club’s financial position and to seek to play at the highest level we will be allowed to play at in the non-league pyramid for the 2027/28 season. We will do it sustainably.”.

#198153. THE BREAKDOWN: The real reasons why Enzo Maresca's Man City can't stop losing - from anonymous Enzo Fernandez abandoning Elliot Anderson, to the fatal flaws in Italian's set-up that are being brutally exposed

THE BREAKDOWN: The real reasons why Enzo Maresca's Man City can't stop losing - from anonymous Enzo Fernandez abandoning Elliot Anderson, to the fatal flaws in Italian's set-up that are being brutally exposed

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 05:23 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Recent findings suggest that diet Pep is losing his fizz.
  • Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a newly introduced manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 05:23 EST, 26 November 2026.

Recent findings suggest that diet Pep is losing his fizz. Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.

Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a newly introduced manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.

Three months in, and three defeats on the spin that left them six points behind Arsenal have made it clear that something is not clicking for Maresca.

Is the uncertainty around the potential punishment following that guilty verdict taking its toll? Is Maresca just suffering from his usual late autumn dips? He suffered similar tricky periods around late October and early November at Leicester and his first season at Chelsea too.

Or is there something at the heart of his side, of his system, that’s finally being exposed?

Enzo Maresca's Man City have slumped to three straight Premier League defeats after a promising start to the season.

Guardiola’s City was all about control. Keep the ball, dominate the pitch, play the game at your pace, on your terms.

Sources indicate that maresca’s City, regardless of how well they started the season, has been about anything but. It has been about triumph amid chaos, about moments of magic more than the overarching method.

Sources indicate that without that control, City’s defensive problems have been laid bare. The 13 goals they have let in after 10 games is their most at this stage since 2008. They haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last eight matches in all competitions. That's a drought longer than at any point under Guardiola.

Their biggest problem over City's three successive Premier League defeats is just how susceptible they have been to counter attacks.

Only Newcastle have faced more shots this season following ‘fast breaks’ – data giants Opta's term for counter attacks – than City’s 17, and 11 of those have come in the last three games: six against Nottingham Forest, two of which led to goals, three against Brighton and another two against Aston Villa.

Industry observers note that maresca’s side are being more profligate in possession, too. Over the first seven games of the season, they lost the ball 120 times a game on average – one of the best figures in the division. Since then, it’s closer to 140.

City have been wasteful in possession and regularly overrun on the counter, with Elliot Anderson (centre) too often left isolated in midfield.

ANDERSON CAN'T DO IT ALL ON HIS OWN.

Industry observers note that many of these problems have their roots in Maresca's serious problems in midfield. Rodri, the best holding midfielder of his generation, was always going to be hard to replace but Maresca appears to be expecting Elliot Anderson to do it all on his own.

Anderson is at his best when he’s free to get up and down the pitch, box to box, using his physicality not just in winning the ball back but progressing it. No midfielder played more passes into the final third last season than Anderson at Forest. At one stage of the campaign, he had played more progressive passes than any other player across Europe’s top five leagues.

And yet Maresca is forcing Anderson to play as the sitter while his golden boy Enzo Fernandez, whom he pushed City to sign in the summer for £125million, is roaming free and high up the pitch.

Maresca likes his teams to build up in a 3-1-6 shape, which sees Fernandez push up as an extra attacking midfielder, and leaves Anderson manning the fort alone.

When City lose the ball, though, it leaves them wide open.

This is the opening goal City conceded against Forest. Josko Gvardiol wants to play the ball inside but has only red shirts and empty green space ahead of him. Anderson is the only man free, but even he is too high and has a Forest player ready to cut off the pass. Eventually, Gvardiol gets robbed and Forest score.

Industry observers note that A lack of options for Josko Gvardiol (left) led to Forest's opener against City. Enzo Fernandez (circled) was caught high up the pitch, way ahead of the deeper Anderson (also circled).

Here’s another moment in the defeat by Brighton.

The Seagulls break forward on the flank and Anderson races over to close the ball down. Fernandez is, you guessed it, high up the pitch.

City have no midfield cover to stop the ball inside, Abdukodir Khusanov gets drawn in and leaves loads of space in behind for Yasin Ayari to exploit and cross to Maxim De Cuyper for a great chance.

The lack of protection offered by Anderson and especially the more advanced Fernandez was again on show against Brighton, who were able to exploit the acres of space left in midfield.

In a recent development, fernandez is doing what Maresca wants, but it’s not working. Maresca needs more from him, especially when Anderson’s instincts are to press and harass and bully, which can leave gaps when he does not yet read the game as comprehensively as Rodri.

According to recent reports, anderson sits in the top five for ball recoveries among midfielders to have played 500 minutes this season. Fernandez is in the bottom five. That figure becomes even more alarming when you consider Anderson has created more chances from open play than Fernandez, too.

Ayyoub Bouaddi indicated at the World Cup that he had the most similar profile to Rodri. It might be time for Maresca to put some faith in him.

Sources indicate that maresca has always wanted his goalkeeper to be an 11th outfielder. In his one season at Leicester, Mads Hermansen played more passes than any goalkeeper in Championship history. During his time at Chelsea, there was a shaky moment in a draw with Arsenal when loud groans greeted a misplaced pass from Robert Sanchez.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I am the guy who asks Robert to do that,’ said Maresca after that game. ‘The moment he stops doing that, he is not going to play.’.

According to recent reports, donnarumma, though, for all his (usually) excellent shot-stopping, is anything but a ball-playing goalkeeper. The ball rolled under his foot from a simple back pass against Coventry and so nearly crept over the line. He gifted France an early lead while on international duty with Italy when he passed the ball straight to Michael Olise.

Only two keepers made more errors leading to shots than Donnarumma across the course of last season, with many of those being with his feet, like when he gifted Kai Havertz an equaliser in City's victory over Arsenal in April.

Gianluigi Donnarumma has never been good with his feet - now his excellent shot-stopping has taken a dip too.

The Italian should have easily dealt with Nicolas Jackson's second goal in City's 2-1 loss at Aston Villa.

The decision to let James Trafford leave in the summer, especially with Guardiola’s impending departure and a manager like Maresca coming in, is looking ever more misguided.

In a recent development, trafford is not immune to mistakes either, of course. He erred badly when trying to play out from the back for City against Spurs last season and made an almost identical howler for Leeds at Bournemouth in October. But he is still far more confident at playing out from the back than Donnarumma.

The double blow for Maresca is that the trade-off with Donnarumma – where he makes up for his weakness with the ball at his feet by making saves that other keepers can’t make – is no longer paying off either.

Nicolas Jackson’s shot squirmed straight through him to hand Villa victory and condemn City to their first defeat of the season.

When you are coughing up chances as frequently as City are, Maresca needs his keeper to be on top form.

Do you know who is keeping the ball out of his net? James Trafford. He boasts the highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in the top flight, keeping out 81 per cent of the shots on target coming his way. Donnarumma is 15th, on less than 66 per cent.

In a recent development, according to Opta’s expected data, Trafford has also prevented more than four goals that he should have conceded from the quality of the shots he’s faced. Again, he’s the best in the Premier League. Donnarumma is middle of the pack.

‘At the moment, I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation,’ said Maresca recently. Without Trafford there and just 34-year-old Geronimo Rulli as back-up, he doesn’t really have a choice but to persist with Donnarumma and hope he improves.

When the goals stop flowing for Erling Haaland, City can't mask all their other problems.

So used are we now to seeing the Norwegian on the scoresheet, having notched nine in City’s opening eight matches, that when he goes just two games without a goal it feels as if he’s on a barren spell.

The concern, though, is less down to Haaland and more that City’s build-up in recent weeks is struggling to get him into the game.

According to recent reports, city are finding it more difficult to get Haaland on the ball. His touches per game are falling steadily but, crucially, so are the quality of the chances his team-mates are creating for him.

According to recent reports, haaland had more than one Opta-defined 'big chance' in five of City’s opening seven games. He’s had just one come his way in each of their three defeats.

Recent findings suggest that his expected goals (xG) tally is dropping too. Across City’s winning streak, Haaland’s average xG per match was 0.81. Only once, against Liverpool, did it drop below 0.5.

Over the three defeats, it’s just 0.45 and has not once gone above 0.5.

Antoine Semenyo missing the last three games through injury has not helped, especially when teams now try to pack the middle of the pitch and force City wide.

Haaland will come good, he always does, but City need to start serving him again if Maresca wants to get through this tricky spell and stop the vultures from circling.

  • Racing de Santander will be bidding to continue their excellent run of form when they head to Estadi Ciutat de Valencia on Friday evening to tackle Levante.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 12:48, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 12:50.

Racing de Santander will be bidding to continue their excellent run of form when they head to Estadi Ciutat de Valencia on Friday evening to tackle Levante.

Levante just about lead the overall head-to-head record between these two sides, winning 11 of their 30 meetings in all competitions, suffering 10 defeats in the process.

Levante have a record of two wins, six draws and five defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them down in 15th spot in the La Liga table.

The Frogs have been an entertaining watch at home this season, scoring 14 times and conceding 13, boasting a record of two wins, two draws and two defeats.

Luis Castro's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-1 draw with Elche, while they also drew 0-0 with Celta Vigo before the November international break, with their last victory coming at home to Athletic Bilbao on October 21.

Levante finished 16th in Spain's top flight last season, so there is clear room for improvement in 2026-27, but they have found it difficult to win matches so far this term.

The Frogs actually beat Racing 3-1 in the last match between the two teams in April 2025, but two of their last four meetings have been won by the latter.

Racing, who are the reigning Segunda Division champions, have been one of the stories of the season in Spain's top flight, impressing hugely on their return to La Liga.

The Green and Whites boast a record of five wins, two draws and six defeats from their 13 league matches, which has left them seventh in the table on 17 points.

Jose Alberto's side have actually conceded 32 times in La Liga this season, which is comfortably the worst record in the division, but they have found the back of the net on 20 occasions - the sixth-best attacking record at this stage.

Racing will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 win over Real Sociedad, and they have now been victorious in three of their last four in the league, and four of their last five in all competitions.

The Green and Whites have struggled away from home this season, though, losing five of their six league matches, only managing to pick up three points.

Racing de Santander form (all competitions):.

Levante lost Jeremy Toljan to an injury in the early stages of their clash with Elche last time out, and the defender is set to miss out on Friday.

The hosts have not reported any further problems, so aside from Nacho Perez coming in for Toljan at right-back, it could be the same side that started the team's last game.

Roger Brugue has scored five times and registered one assist in 13 appearances this season, and the 30-year-old is again set for a spot in the starting side.

Karl Etta Eyong, though, is likely to start on the bench.

As for Racing, Maguette Gueye, Alvaro Mantilla and Andres Martin could potentially miss the match through injury, but the visitors are otherwise in strong shape.

Yassir Zabiri, who is on loan at the club from Rennes, has been in excellent form this season, scoring 11 times in 13 league appearances, and he will again feature in the final third of the field.

There should also be another spot in the first XI for the experienced Sergio Canales, who has been a key player for the club this term at the age of 35, coming up with two goals and one assist in 13 appearances.

Levante possible starting lineup:.

Ryan; Perez, Mandi, Dela, Sanchez; Rey; Brugue, Requena, Olasagasti, Fernandez; Romero.

Racing de Santander possible starting lineup:.

Agirrezabala; Ramon, Felipe, Belocian, Salinas; Prati, I Martin; Luque, Canales, Vicente; Zabiri.

Racing have struggled away from home this season, but the visitors are in excellent form, and we are expecting them to be good enough for a point in this match.

#198151. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea
