Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4587 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.
  • Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.
  • In a recent development, alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

In a recent development, alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

Recent findings suggest that when it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”.

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

According to recent reports, it looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

In a recent development, cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”.

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

It has been revealed that TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

Industry observers note that reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Industry observers note that reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who mentioned: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

Recent findings suggest that “I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”.

Recent findings suggest that goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk.

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav.

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Industry observers note that any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were quickly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

It has been revealed that on the defeat by Chelsea, Farke noted: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

In a recent development, “All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”.

In a recent development, "100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers says he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla.

Here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk.

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

It has been revealed that asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he said: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”.

Sources indicate that on Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady mentioned on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the substantial guns came on... They were electric at times.”.

A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Sources indicate that palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

It has been revealed that fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

Rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

It has been revealed that chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

Shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

In a recent development, leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Industry observers note that chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9.

We could be in for a blockbuster finish.

Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

Recent findings suggest that chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

In a recent development, it will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz.

Palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

Chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

Industry observers note that "This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX.

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

It has been revealed that chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

Sources indicate that TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6.

Chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ.

Recent findings suggest that chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Industry observers note that chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav.

Sources indicate that alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

It has been revealed that massive cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:.

Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Paris St-Germain 4 Slovan 0Napoli 0 Arsenal 0Sporting CP 1 Galatasaray 1.

Boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

There is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

Recent findings suggest that justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

Better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

Gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

Gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

According to recent reports, farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

Recent findings suggest that massive chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

Industry observers note that leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu launches a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 1 (Muharemovic) Set-pieces have been a massive feature of Leeds’ game this season and here they take the lead with the simplest of corner routines. Wilson floats the ball to the back post where Muharemovic is waiting, unmarked, and he loops a header over Penders into the net. Such a shame for the Chelsea keeper as he had just pulled off a stunning double-save.

"The set-piece routine does it again!" Tarik Muharemović puts Leeds in front against Chelsea! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/UxeJ3xgL56.

Industry observers note that barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

There is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as big as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

Major chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

In a recent development, gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

Leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

A couple of early touches for Watson who plays a neat pass around the corner. Ampadu then lands a late tackle on Lacroix and Chelsea earn a free-kick in their own half.

Although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

According to recent reports, chelsea and Leeds emerge from the tunnel, led out by Colwill and former Chelsea defender Ampadu. Here’s a reminder of the teams in full:.

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck.

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro.

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha.

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya.

Daniel Farke believes Leeds can go far in the Carabao Cup this year 💪 pic.twitter.com/26ueAAUHoZ.

Recent findings suggest that on the Brazilian winger’s opportunity tonight, Hasselbaink said on Sky Sports: “He has to find his place. This is his opportunity... It’s not really an out-and-out left-wing [position] or a No 10 as he can play, but [with] good players it doesn’t matter where you put them on the pitch. He will find his spaces and he will be direct as he was when he came in against Arsenal. He is going to play for his place because he wants to play week-in, week-out.”.

"He deserves to be there because of what he has shown" Xabi Alonso speaks about Reggie Watson with the 16-year-old set to make his Chelsea debut in their Carabao Cup game against Leeds 🌟 pic.twitter.com/AAn4Av3iEh.

According to recent reports, tfl has closed South Kensington station after a “customer incident” meaning parts of the District Line have closed. The decision was then made to delay the match to give supporters more time to get to the stadium.

Reggie Watson will become the fourth youngest player, aged 16, in Chelsea’s history. But he will have to wait a little bit longer for his debut as kick-off has been delayed by 15 minutes to 8.15pm.

There will be a 15 minute delay to kick-off for our Carabao Cup third round tie with Leeds United tonight. The match will now begin at 20:15 BST. pic.twitter.com/MdDXpxgW09.

A couple of cracking strikes from the Dutchman. Some player he was...

"Good old days!" Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink reflects on his goals for Leeds against Chelsea 🎞️ pic.twitter.com/bYjyFYIVIK.

ChelseaAug 24: Fulham 2 Chelsea 3Aug 27: Chelsea 2 Luton Town 0 (Carabao Cup)Aug 30: Chelsea 4 Brighton 3Sep 6: Arsenal 2 Chelsea 1.

LeedsAug 22: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 1Aug 25: Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds 2Aug 30: Leeds 1 Brentford 1Sep 5: Brighton 1 Leeds 1.

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

It has been revealed that estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

Chelsea Penders; Gusto, Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill, Chavarria; Watson, Barco; Estevao, Gittens; Welbeck.

Substitutes Martinez, Hato, Fofana, James, Neto, Palmer, Quenda, Rogers, Pedro.

Leeds United Zetterer; Justin, Bijol, Muharemovic; James, Ampadu, Longstaff, Bard; Wilson, Aaronson; Nmecha.

Substitutes Trafford, Gudmundsson, Elvedi, Bogle, Tanaka, Stach, Okafor, Calvert-Lewin, Bahoya.

Much has been made of Chelsea’s willingness to let the opposition have the ball under Xabi Alonso, but tonight they will likely be forced to dictate proceedings. In Leeds, they face one of only two sides who have completed fewer passes than them in the Premier League.

1. Ian Hamilton in 1967: 16 years, four months and 15 days2. Kingsley Whiffen in 1967: 16 years, five months and six days3. Reggie Walsh in 2025: 16 years, six months and 11 days4. Reggie Watson in 2026: 16 years, seven months and 14 days5. Tommy Langley in 1974: 16 years, nine months and one day.

Recent findings suggest that asked how he will approach the Carabao Cup this season, Daniel Farke said: “We’ll try to win it. That’s the quickest way to Europe and to some glory. Of course knowing that the Premier League will always have the priority and knowing that we are as successful as possible there, especially to reach our first goal to establish ourselves [at] this level.

“We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Challenging, difficult games, but of course we travel to London in order to go through in the next round without doing anything stupid at this stage of the campaign because you also have to rotate a bit more and integrate a few new players. Nevertheless, we want to be at our best and anyhow possible we also want to go through to the next round.”.

Tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. The central-midfielder caught Alonso’s eye during pre-season when the Spaniard said of him: “Reggie Watson, a great midfielder. He thinks, he’s very collective, he’s very generous on the effort, intelligent with the ball”.

“For his age, I’m really impressed with him.”.

Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate upcoming players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

It has been revealed that if Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

It has been revealed that alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

Alphadjo Cisse is one goal away from double figures for the season, and we have not even reached the end of November yet.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, the numbers that Cisse is putting up are those of a centre-forward. He has six goals in 10 Serie A appearances, at an average of one every 74 minutes. In the Europa League he has three (a hat-trick against RB Salzburg), at one every 84 minutes.

Sources indicate that yet, his role remains a bit of a mystery. Cisse has his own idea of ​​his preferred position on the pitch, even if he’s a bit vague. Speaking after the match against Frosinone, he hinted that he’d like to move into the attacking midfielder position behind the striker.

In a recent development, “I’d have more fun and entertain the fans. It would also be easier to provide assists for my team-mates, something I enjoy and haven’t yet managed to do at AC Milan,” he confessed to Sky.

In a recent development, in Verona’s youth team, where Cisse first emerged, head coach Paolo Sammarco deployed him as a left-sided attacking midfielder. It was a position in which the then 17-year-old then went on to score 16 league goals in a breakout season.

At Catanzaro, in his first professional stint in Serie B under Alberto Aquilani, the Italian played more or less the same role in a 3-4-2-1 system, sometimes a bit wider. Before the serious injury that caused him to miss the final six months of last season, he has scored six goals in 22 games.

Industry observers note that ruben Amorim initially deployed him as a left-sided winger, also due to Christian Pulisic’s temporary unavailability. He would later move him further forward and more centrally, to take up the spaces a striker would, a position he has played for Italy U21s under Silvio Baldini.

Industry observers note that in this position, Cisse can utilise his extraordinary ability to position himself between the ball and the defender, before turning, aiming and often finishing first time. Despite not being physically big (at 180cm tall), he is strong and has a low centre of gravity that makes him tough to bump off the ball.

This is where the dilemma arises. At Verona and Catanzaro, Alphadjo Cisse impressed because of his speed and agility. After the injury and under the watch of Amorim, he has become more of a positioning-based player, barely ever tearing down the flank.

So far this season, he’s attempted only 16 dribbles at just over three per game, and has only succeeded on five. With one successful dribble per game on average, his success rate is just over 31% (FotMob data).

These numbers perhaps help explain Cisse’s progression close to the penalty area, and also a concept that the player himself has repeated in recent months regarding where he is at in his personal development. On Sunday, he declared: “I’m not even halfway to my potential.”.

Recent findings suggest that who knows if Alpha is referring to his overall growth, with horizons still unexplored, or perhaps his post-injury recovery. Amorim will continue to ponder things, but this is far from a headache, because the rule seems to be well established: if Cisse plays, he tends to score.

Mikel Arteta states David Raya will undergo more tests on his shoulder injury before Arsenal’s Premier League game against Manchester City on Sunday.

Raya was forced off in the second half of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw away to Newcastle United on Saturday evening.

The Spanish goalkeeper appeared to be in significant discomfort and has been unable to train since Arsenal’s game at St James’ Park.

Kepa Arrizabalaga took Raya’s place in goal for Arsenal’s 2-2 draw at home to Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

But Arteta admits Raya is still an injury doubt for Arsenal’s next Premier League fixture against City at the Emirates Stadium this weekend.

Speaking ahead of kick-off against Dortmund, Arteta told Prime Sport: ‘Again, we need some more tests.

‘He’s evolving well. Obviously, we were very relieved with the news because we feared the worst. But we’ll have to wait and see.’.

When asked after his side’s 2-2 draw with Dortmund, Arteta added: ‘We need to know first how bad it is and whether he has a chance or not in the next few weeks.’.

During his pre-match press conference on Monday, Arteta confirmed that Raya will not need to undergo surgery.

‘We were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected.

‘The doctor explained what happened but it’s quite technical and when you look at the action there doesn’t seem to be much, but the extent of the pain that he had and the pain he had was quite worrying.’.

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 12:59, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 12:59.

Lincoln City have sacked co-managers Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

The pair were promoted from the club's backroom staff after head coach Michael Skubala made the decision to leave the League One champions for Bristol City in the summer.

With Lincoln sitting in 21st place in the Championship table and two points above the relegation zone, a positive spin can be put on the club's first campaign in the second tier of English football for more than 60 years.

However, Tuesday's 4-0 defeat at Charlton Athletic was Lincoln's fifth successive loss in the Championship.

As well as one win and eight defeats being posted across a 10-match period, the club's hierarchy have decided for a change in direction.

A statement read: "We have worked incredibly hard to reach the Championship and will do everything in our power to retain our status in this division.”   "We know how much this football club means to our supporters and are humbled by the level of support we’ve had home and away so far this season.".

ℹ️ City can confirm Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw have been relieved of their duties as head coaches with immediate effect. We thank them for their contributions to the club over the last several years and wish them well for the future. https://t.co/mwLolWdxhp.

Lincoln add that they will next provide an update on their search for a successor to Cohen and Shaw on November 30.

Despite 15 points coming from 17 matches, Cohen and Shaw can have no complaints over Lincoln's decision.

With Preston North End and Burnley - in 22nd and 23rd position - closing the gap, Lincoln's owners are justified in the move that they have taken.

Furthermore, second-placed Wolverhampton Wanderers are the next visitors to the ProAmpac Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

Likely viewing that game as a free-hit under first-team coach Stuart Pearson, Lincoln will look to have a permanent manager in place for the trip to Cardiff City on December 5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rasmus Hojlund told Manchester City fans ‘there is only one club in Manchester’ after scoring for Napoli in their Champions League clash on Tuesday night.

Hojlund scored the opening goal in the second half at the Etihad Stadiumbut City salvaged a 2-2 draw following Rayan Cherki’s equaliser in the 86th minute.

After scoring his first Champions League goal of the season with a brilliant low finish past Gianluigi Donnarumma, Hojlund celebrating in front of City’s supporters.

But before turning to the half way line, the Denmark international held up one finger and told the crowd: ‘There is only one club in Manchester’.

When asked about his celebration after the game, Hojlund stated: ‘Some good banter, you know.

‘There’s the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United and obviously I have a past in Manchester United. That’s my club. Nothing against City but United is my home.’.

Former Red, Rasmus Hojlund scoring at the Etihad tonight:“There’s only one club in Manchester” 🔴⚪️⚫️😍 pic.twitter.com/mS5eQsMWRA.

Hojlund joined Manchester United in a £72 million deal from Atalanta in 2023 and spent two seasons at Old Trafford before his loan move to Napoli.

The 23-year-old then completed a £38 million permanent move to Napoli this summer as the Serie A club had an obligation to sign him after qualifying for the Champions League.

During his two seasons at United, Hojlund scored 26 goals in 95 appearances.

Erling Haaland admits Manchester City are ‘not clicking fully’ and believes his side now face the ‘most difficult game of the season’ against Arsenal this weekend.

City have now registered just two wins in their last seven games in all competitions after they came from behind twice to draw 2-2 at home to Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

Haaland, meanwhile, endured another frustrating game as he failed to find the net and the Norway international registered just one shot on target against Napoli.

‘We managed to come back two times but we demand more, we have to do better, we have to find some ways to make us control the game more and perform in a better way,’ Haaland told beIN Sports after City’s draw at the Etihad Stadium.

‘I have no idea what we were missing, but you could feel it in the last few games that there’s something that’s not clicking fully and we have to find out and we have to stay positive and we have to get the best out of every single player.’.

It has been revealed that in a separate post-match interview, Haaland added: ‘Football is so easy and so difficult. When you win games everything is easy and you know what to do, and when you don’t win you start to question everything. The perfect thing to do is don’t think.

By Saikat Mandal | 25 Nov 2026 13:05, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 13:05.

Liverpool are reportedly keeping a close eye on Borussia Dortmund youngster Joane Gadou.

The 19-year-old joined the German club in the summer transfer window from Red Bull Salzburg and has already made a strong impression at his newly introduced side.

The youngster has made 10 Bundesliga appearances, starting nine of them, while also featuring five times in the Champions League.

According to CaughtOffside's The Daily Briefing, Liverpool are among the clubs showing keen interest in the young centre-back, who is also capable of operating at right-back.

The Reds could face competition from Manchester United and Arsenal for Gadou, while Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain are also monitoring his progress.

Gadou is particularly strong in the air and has already produced several eye-catching performances, with his display in the 1-1 draw against Arsenal attracting considerable attention.

The report claims that although several top clubs are keeping a close watch on his development, none are at the moment ready to make a move for him.

The Frenchman is under contract at Dortmund until 2031, and while a departure could become a possibility at some point in the future, a move is not expected in the immediate term.

Liverpool will probably need to sign a newly introduced centre-back next summer, with Joe Gomez potentially heading for the exit.

With Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni, the Reds already have two highly talented young centre-backs, and there would be little harm in further strengthening their pool of promising defensive prospects.

Virgil van Dijk has been outstanding once again this season and is showing few signs that age is beginning to catch up with him.

Liverpool should certainly continue monitoring Gadou's progress for the remainder of the campaign, and if an opportunity arises, taking a chance on him as a potential long-term replacement for Gomez could prove worthwhile.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Villa were beaten 1-0 in Turkey and now sit ninth in the Champions League table, one place outside the automatic qualification spots.
  • Garnacho, meanwhile, trained with his Villa teammates on Monday but he was not even named on the bench against Galatasaray.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery delivered a blunt assessment of Alejandro Garnacho’s situation at Aston Villa after the Argentine was left out of the squad for the defeat to Galatasaray on Tuesday night.

Villa were beaten 1-0 in Turkey and now sit ninth in the Champions League table, one place outside the automatic qualification spots.

Garnacho, meanwhile, trained with his Villa teammates on Monday but he was not even named on the bench against Galatasaray.

The on-loan Chelsea winger was also not included in Villa’s squad for their goalless draw at home to Sunderland on Saturday.

For the game against Galatasaray, Emery only picked 11 substitutes out of a possible 12 and also included two goalkeepers.

When asked about Garnacho’s absence after Villa’s defeat, Emery replied: ‘Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us, to play with us.’.

Garnacho has made just seven appearances since joining Villa in the summer and is yet to score a goal or register an assist.

Villa have an obligation to buy Garnacho from Chelsea for £43 million but only if he makes a certain number of appearances this season.

Chelsea signed Garnacho in a £40m deal from Manchester United last year but the Argentine struggled to make an impact during his time at Stamford Bridge, scoring eight goals in 43 appearances.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool have successfully negotiated the option to sign Senegal wonderkid Sidy Barhama Ndiaye once he turns 18.

Ndiaye, currently 16, trialled with Liverpool’s academy in the summer of 2025 and now has a clear pathway to Merseyside.

Per reports from The Athletic, the Reds have pipped a number of European rivals to get right of first refusal for his signing in January 2028.

English clubs cannot sign players from overseas until they have turned 18, which Ndiaye will do on New Year’s Eve in 2027.

Ndiaye at the moment plies his trade in his home nation with Diambars FC, whom he helped earn promotion to the Senegalese top flight last season.

Ndiaye is currently away at the Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, picking up a goal and two assists in a 9-0 drubbing of Cuba earlier this week.

Sources indicate that senegal’s only other match at the tournament so far resulted in a 1-1 draw with Croatia. Liverpool fans hoping to get a glimpse of a future star, though, might be tempted to tune into their meeting with Tajikistan on Thursday, November 26.

Liverpool have made a habit of spotting talent at such tournaments. At last year’s U17 World Cup, their scouts brought home Senegal’s Mor Talla Ndiaye, Austria’s Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Belgium’s Lucca Brughmans.

It remains to be seen whether Liverpool will opt to sign Ndiaye in 2028, and what role he might play at the club if they do.

Ndiaye will hope to follow in the footsteps of one of Liverpool’s all-time greats, his countryman Sadio Mane, in making the move to the north-west.

Jamie Carragher believes Arsenal will beat Manchester City to end their Premier League title hopes on Sunday, while Thierry Henry claims Enzo Maresca’s side are ‘there to be dominated’.

Arsenal sit six points clear of City at the top of the Premier League and head into this weekend’s fixture off the back of a 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

City, meanwhile, have registered just two wins in their last seven games in all competitions and needed to come from behind twice to draw 2-2 with Napoli in their Champions League game on Tuesday.

Enzo Maresca’s side visit the Emirates Stadium this weekend and Carragher feels Arsenal will be too strong for their Premier League title rivals.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I think Arsenal will win. I can’t see City getting anything from that game,’ Carragher told CBS Sports after Arsenal’s draw with Dortmund.

‘They’ve been really poor of late, the results have shown that, not strong defensively at all.

‘Arsenal in the last couple of games have let in a couple of goals but I think they’ll be really tuned in to know if they beat Manchester City that’ll be end of Manchester City in terms of the title.

‘I think they’ll be really aggressive, man-to-man press, get after them all over the pitch. I just don’t see them [City] at all.’.

Asked who he believes can challenge Arsenal for the title, Carragher replied: ‘No one.

‘And that’s not because Arsenal are amazing. Listen, they are a top team, don’t get me wrong, but in terms of the Champions League, I don’t think the Premier League teams can match… only Arsenal can really match what we’re seeing from the top teams.

The money we’ve got, the teams that we have, we have major four or five teams who would all think they all have a real opportunity each season to win the league, spend big money, hundreds of millions on individual players, my own team being one in Liverpool. So to see how far we all are behind, besides Arsenal, they got to the Champions League final last season, you see City tonight, you see Villa lose, Liverpool lost a couple of weeks ago away to Fenerbahce.

In a recent development, ‘I still think you’ve almost got four or five teams, Arsenal are one of them, the massive teams in the Champions League. For the Premier League not to have more than one, considering we’ve got five in the competition and the funds they all have, it’s probably a bit disappointing and shows why Arsenal are favourites for the Premier League.’.

Meanwhile, Thierry Henry believes City’s run of form shows that Maresca’s side could struggle to control the game against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

‘You have two teams who have to rectify two things at the weekend – Arsenal, like we’ve been saying recently, and Mikel Arteta has been saying, when you’re on top of a team, don’t let them come back to attack like we’ve seen in the last two games,’ Henry remarked.

‘If you go back to City, and I’ve remarked it since the beginning of the season, the balance of the team isn’t right. Simple as that.

‘That didn’t stop them losing games under Pep [Guardiola] but they were more in control of games.

Sources indicate that ‘You have two teams who have been dominating the league in the last two, three years. But I want to see an Arsenal team that’s going to dominate City, and they are there to be dominated.

‘But on the other side, it might be the day that City wake up. But if they play the same way they’ve been playing recently, being open and all over the place in midfield, it could be a long day.’.

By Saikat Mandal | 25 Nov 2026 13:41.

Brentford defender Nathan Collins is reportedly high on Manchester United's list of targets for the January transfer window.

Mauricio Pochettino's managerial debut at Man Utd ended in disappointment as the Red Devils suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat against Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League.

With the side languishing in 19th place in the Premier League table, a major squad overhaul is required in January, although reports suggest Pochettino may not be handed a substantial transfer budget.

Nevertheless, signing an experienced centre-back and a striker remains a priority for the Red Devils, with Collins emerging as a potential option.

According to a report from talkSPORT, the Red Devils are prioritising ready-made defenders, and Collins fits the profile they are looking for.

The 25-year-old joined Brentford from Wolverhampton Wanderers in the summer of 2023 and has since made 124 appearances for the club, scoring eight goals.

Collins is under contract with Brentford until the summer of 2029, meaning the Bees are likely to demand a sizeable transfer fee.

Furthermore, the Bees are pushing for European qualification this season and may be reluctant to part ways with one of their key players midway through the campaign.

The Red Devils have also been linked with a move for Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey in January, but they may need to act rapidly if they are serious about securing his services.

Bassey recently confirmed that he has been negotiating a newly introduced contract with the Cottagers, potentially leaving Man Utd at risk of missing out on the defender.

The Red Devils have also been long-term admirers of Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite, although the Toffees are expected to demand a substantial fee for their prized asset.

Pochettino may not have the luxury of spending heavily on a single player and could therefore need to offload some fringe players to free up squad space and generate funds for latest arrivals.

The Walcott has urged Arsenal star Noni Madueke to ‘big himself up more’ after Mikel Arteta revealed last night’s man of the match was frustrated in the wake of a 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund.

For the second match in succession, the Premier League champions threw away a lead and squandered numerous chances to record a convincing win.

Viktor Gyokeres opened the scoring with a blistering strike in the 10th minute, but the Sweden international, like many of his teammates, was profligate thereafter.

Ultimately, the Gunners were forced to settle for a point following Maximilian Beier’s second half equaliser and Mikel Arteta’s side are now likely to require two wins from their remaining three group stage games to secure a top eight finish and avoid a two-legged play-off in the Newly introduced Year.

Industry observers note that madueke, meanwhile, walked away with the man of the match accolade after another lively display. The England international has been to the fore in recent weeks and, in the absence of Bukayo Saka, appears to have won the faith of the manager who raised eyebrows with his decision to sanctionthe decision to sign him from Chelsea in a £52million deal 18 months ago.

The 24-year-old was, however, far from pleased with a display that failed to help yield a win that Arsenal’s dominance deserved, according to Arteta.

‘Again he was really good, but if you were in the dressing room (you would see) he is not satisfied because he knows he had so many situations again that we can put the ball in the net or finish the action much better,’ said the Arsenal boss.

It has been revealed that ‘But again he was a real threat, he was super connected to the game with and without the ball. He was a real threat.’.

Walcott, meanwhile, agreed with his former Arsenal teammate and believes Madueke is showing signs that he is capable of maintaining a regular starting spot.

By Saikat Mandal | 25 Nov 2026 14:15.

Bournemouth have slapped a hefty price tag on Eli Junior Kroupi as they maintain that the forward is not for sale in the January transfer window.

The 20-year-old joined the Cherries last summer from Lorient and has made 35 appearances for the club across all competitions, scoring 13 goals.

His impressive form has not gone unnoticed, with several top clubs, including Arsenal, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, taking a keen interest in signing him.

According to a report from talkSPORT, Bournemouth have no intention of selling their prized asset in the January transfer window.

The Cherries are fifth in the Premier League table and will be chasing a place in the Champions League next season, making them unlikely to part ways with any of their key players midway through the campaign.

They are determined to keep hold of the 20-year-old until at least the summer and have slapped a whopping £100m price tag on his head.

Kroupi is under contract until the summer of 2030 and reportedly favours a move to La Liga champions Barcelona if a transfer materialises in the future.

Arsenal are looking to bolster their attacking options in the January window, with signing a versatile winger a priority for Mikel Arteta.

The Gunners have followed Kroupi's progress closely, but whether they would be willing to spend upwards of £100m on the youngster remains a major question.

Moreover, Arsenal have been monitoring other options and could turn to relatively cheaper alternatives, such as Antonio Nusa.

The north London club have also reportedly joined Real Madrid in the race for an ambitious move for Bayern Munich superstar Michael Olise, although a potential January transfer is out of the question.

In any case, the Gunners will likely have to spend substantial to secure a top-class winger, and while Kroupi could be an ideal addition, prising him away from Bournemouth in January looks a difficult proposition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino will not be able to call on Matheus Cunha as he chases his first win with Manchester United.

The Red Devils’ new boss is facing just his second match in charge of the club as he looks to bounce back from the weekend’s chastening 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

He will return to the Champions League for the first time since leaving Paris Saint-Germain this evening, with a tricky tie away at Sporting on the docket.

However, in a selection blow, he will not be able to make use of one of his more threatening forwards, with Cunha left out of the Lisbon-bound travelling squad.

There was some positive news in the squad, though, as Luke Shaw and Karl Darlow came back into contention after injury layoffs, but the absence of Cunha is a serious setback for Pochettino as he looks to breathe life into his nascent United tenure.

Matheus Cunha was left out of the travelling squad for Manchester United’s meeting with Sporting as he is serving a red card suspension.

The Brazilian forward was dismissed in second-half injury time as United came from behind to beat Roma 3-2 last time out in the Champions League.

Having trailed by two goals to nil with just 17 minutes played, a second-half penalty from Bruno Fernandes and a quickfire brace from Cunha flipped the script.

Cunha, though, was shown two yellow cards in a chaotic finish.

The first came when he removed his shirt celebrating what proved to be the winning goal, and he picked up a second in the 91st minute for a needless, reckless late tackle on Leonardo Balerdi.

Cunha is only suspended for one match.

He will serve his suspension against Sporting tonight and be available again when United host RB Leipzig in two weeks’ time, on December 8.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jobe Bellingham revealed one of Borussia Dortmund’s coaches was responsible for identifying a ‘mismatch’ that helped his side earn a valuable Champions League point against Arsenal.

The Gunners could’ve been out of sight at half-time but had only Viktor Gyokeres’ spectacular early goal to show for their superiority.

Bundesliga table toppers Dortmund, were a different side immediately after the break and claimed a deserved equaliser through Maximilian Beier.

Dortmund’s physical approach and man-to-man system gradually saw them take control and they were millimeters from taking the lead when Bellingham was ruled offside and saw his close-range effort disallowed.

The 21-year-old was substituted shortly afterwards as was the Arsenal star he had be targeting having been instructed to make the most of a physical mismatch.

‘One of the coaches pointed out to me that I was against Myles [Lewis-Skelly],’ he explained on Amazon Prime Video.

‘For the long ball – I don’t want to say a mismatch – but I’m obviously bigger.

Jobe Bellingham's goal RULED OUT for offside ❌ pic.twitter.com/yaR8EX4Gs3.

‘You would expect that if I was against Gabriel or Ezri [Konsa] it would be a bit more difficult to win the long balls.

‘I thought that there was a bit of an advantage there in terms of height. I managed to win a few flick-ons and get us up the pitch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has explained his decision to hand Joshua Zirkzee a first start of the season against Sporting in the Champions League.

The Argentine named just his second United team in Lisbon on Wednesday evening as he looked to bounce back from a damning 4-0 defeat by Liverpool on his managerial bow.

In Portugal, he made four changes from the side he named at Anfield, with Harry Maguire, Noussair Mazraoui and Amad Diallo all coming into the side.

Perhaps his most notable call, though, saw striker Zirkzee chosen to lead the line, making his first start of the campaign.

The Dutchman has been bumped up the pecking order somewhat for this match, with fellow striker Benjamin Sesko out injured and deputy Matheus Cunha suspended.

Pochettino, though, said he hopes Zirkzee can kick on as a more dependable option, given United’s thin ranks.

According to recent reports, asked to explain the selection, he told TNT Sports: “Cunha is suspended, of course, Sesko is injured. I think it is a great opportunity for Josh (Zirkzee) to show his quality.

“I think it is an key game to start to think that he can be a very important player for the team, and today is an opportunity for him.”.

Zirkzee was entirely peripheral under Michael Carrick and had looked to leave United in the summer transfer window. He was the subject of a loan bid from Everton on Deadline Day, but no move materialised.

Pochettino, though, seems optimistic he can bring Zirkzee in from the cold as United look to salvage their campaign, both domestically and abroad.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:16, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:19.

On Friday, the Columbus Crew can pull off what may become the biggest upset in MLS playoff history and eliminate Inter Miami in game two of that first-round series at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

Last weekend the Crew took game one by a 3-0 score, putting them in position to eliminate the reigning champions should they win this upcoming fixture.

Columbus had a lot of momentum heading into the playoffs, and that continued on Saturday as they took advantage of some sloppy Miami defending to take a surprising lead in this series.

Laurent Courtois has seen his side score three or more goals in four of their last five matches versus MLS opposition, while posting a clean sheet in three of those instances, making them an appealing option to choose on the UK betting sites.

The Crew exposed gaps in the Miami squad, scoring on three of their five targeted efforts last weekend and putting the Herons on the ropes heading into game two.

This is only the second time they are up 1-0 since this best-of-three first-round format was introduced, with this team advancing past Atlanta United in three games on the only previous occasion in which they were in this position in 2023.

Only once since their 2015 MLS Cup final defeat versus the Portland Timbers have they lost a post-season match at home, with the New York Red Bulls blanking them 1-0 in game one of that opening round series in 2024.

Friday will mark the second time the Crew can eliminate Miami from a major competition in Columbus, after knocking them out of the 2024 Leagues Cup thanks to a 3-2 victory at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in the round of 16.

For a team boasting so much experience and talent in the biggest club and international competitions, Inter Miami failed to keep their composure in numerous instances last weekend.

Saturday’s defeat was the joint-worst for the club in the post-season, though given everything that transpired, they could be looking much worse heading into this match.

Kily Gonzalez will be relieved to know that Lionel Messi is available, escaping with just a caution in game one after throwing the ball at Gonzalo Tapia, a moment some believed should have warranted a sending off for the Argentine.

Miami played a good portion of that match a man down, and have never won the second game in a best-of-three MLS playoff series.

The Herons have given up a combined six goals in their last two matches versus MLS opposition and have yet to beat an MLS club in a knockout fixture this season.

The reigning league champions have lost four of their five all-time playoff outings away from home, with their only triumph coming at FC Cincinnati in 2025 (4-0).

Columbus Crew form (all competitions):.

Inter Miami Major League Soccer form:.

Due to a cruciate ligament tear, Wessam Abou Ali will not be available for Columbus in game two of this series.

Gonzalo Tapia netted twice in Miami, with Taha Habroune also scoring as Patrick Schulte made three stops for the clean sheet.

On the Miami side, Mateo Silvetti is dealing with a shoulder issue, Tadeo Allende still has a knee problem and Israel Boatwright is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Gonzalo Lujan will be suspended following his red card in game one, while Sergio Reguilon, David Ayala and Cesar Abadia are all questionable with lower-body injuries.

Columbus Crew possible starting lineup:.

Schulte; Farsi, Moreira, Zawadzki, Amundsen; Zaroury, Chambost, Habroune, Rodriguez, Tapia, Mendez.

Inter Miami possible starting lineup:.

It has been revealed that st. Clair; Fray, Casemiro, Micael, Falcon; De Paul, Bright, Segovia; Messi, Suarez, Berterame.

While Miami have all they need to come back and win this series, they are far too rigid defensively and give away too many quality scoring opportunities, which is why we believe their season will end much earlier than most would have expected.

Former Chelsea and England star Shaun Wright-Phillips has urged Estevao to fight tooth and nail for a starting spot at Stamford Bridge and make himself ‘hard to ignore’ under Xabi Alonso.

Estevao burst onto the scene across an eye-catching opening campaign with Chelsea having joined the club from Palmeiras in the summer of 2025, racking up eight goals and four assists for the Blues.

A serious hamstring tear brought Estevao’s debut season to a premature end, though, a devastating blow that saw him miss out on a place in Brazil’s squad at this year’s World Cup.

Just days after Estevao sustained his injury, Chelsea decided to call time on Liam Rosenior’s turbulent managerial spell – and it has proven difficult for the 19-year-old to work himself back into the side since Alonso took charge.

The teenager had been limited to only two starts in the Carabao Cup approaching late October and rumours were beginning to circulate that he had grown frustrated with his peripheral role, with Barcelona reportedly keeping tabs on the situation.

However, Joao Pedro’s absence over the last month-and-a-half has created an opportunity for Estevao in Alonso’s attack and the youngster has started two of Chelsea’s last three games.

A humbling 4-1 defeat at the hands of Leeds may not have been what Estevao had in mind for his return, though, following a substitute appearance at Sunderland, and he will no doubt be desperate to banish those memories with a strong performance versus Nottingham Forest on Friday night.

Asked if he felt that Estevao still had a big future at Chelsea under Alonso, Wright-Phillips told Metro, courtesy of kwiff: ‘It’s a hard one, because it seems like players at Chelsea outlive the managers, which is sad to say.

Recent findings suggest that ‘That’s where modern football is going at the minute. It seems like players are outlasting coaches.

‘But in general, that’s more of a tactical thing, in that Xabi plays more with wing-backs.

‘If you play Estevao, you want him in the front three. Chances come in random ways, so he will get his chance again, and he has to do what he did the other day.

‘When he came on, I thought he was flying: not the weekend just gone, the weekend before that [against Sunderland. He came on and played really, really well.

‘So that’s him saying, “Look, I’m good enough to stay in your squad.” If he continuously does that, it becomes hard to ignore.’.

Another player whose development has hit something of a stumbling block in recent months is Malo Gusto, who, like Estevao, has found regular game-time hard to come by this season.

Reports just last week indicated Gusto could be open to the prospect of leaving Chelsea, with Manchester United understood to be among the right-back’s admirers.

But when asked if it could be time to move Gusto on should a suitable offer come in for the Frenchman, Wright-Phillips replied: ‘Who do you replace him with? I think Gusto is a really fantastic player.

‘He might not be happy, which is understandable, because before Xabi came, when the other managers were there, his playing time was a lot greater, because it was either him or Reece James.

‘Reece James has had bad luck, he’s injured quite a lot, so Gusto got to play a lot. Whereas now, I think he’s better than a bit-part player, to be honest.

‘I haven’t watched him enough this season to turn around and say he should definitely be starting, but from what I saw of him last year and the type of player he is, I’d have him in my team at the drop of a hat, because I don’t think there are many right-backs out there that are gettable of that standard.’.

Chelsea splashed out in the region of £350million on new signings in the summer transfer window, including Morgan Rogers, who commanded a club-record fee of £117m when he joined from Aston Villa.

There were signs that the Blues were reaping the rewards of their significant spending in a promising start to the 2026/27 campaign, with Alonso’s all-star front three firing on all cylinders.

An injury to Joao Pedro has coincided with a concerning dip in results, though, and Alonso’s men were targeted with a chorus of boos as they exited the pitch following their latest setback on Saturday.

Sources indicate that ‘I think at the very beginning he showed why he’s there, and at the minute it seems to have plateaued a bit. I don’t know what that’s from,’ Wright-Phillips said when asked what he had made of Alonso’s start to managerial life in the Premier League, with Chelsea languishing down in eighth.

‘Playing as many games as they have, with the internationals that have come in the way they’ve come in, it feels like the Champions League is every week; it feels like it’s the Carabao Cup or something every week at the minute.

‘It’s going to take a bit of time for the players to get used to that change, where every game is a significant game now for everybody; literally every game comes around very quick.

‘I think those clubs will settle down and get it together because they’re lucky to have the players within that squad to do that.’.

It has been revealed that pressed on whether there were any areas of the squad in need of strengthening in January, Wright-Phillips responded: ‘I’m not sure they need midfielders. I would say if they had two, or even one, solid defenders who can teach the other young ones there, that would be more than enough.

Sources indicate that ‘Chelsea have got an amazing squad. They’re missing that rock at the back; who will fight and die for everybody, because that rubs off on the team.

In a recent development, ‘You might not like him, but that attitude and mentality will naturally rub off on you. Someone in the Thiago Silva mould.

Industry observers note that ‘They need to learn; they’re learning from each other. They’re good players, but to get to the top, most younger players and defenders learn off somebody with a lot more experience.’.

Switching his focus to the title race, Wright-Phillips, who represented Manchester City, Chelsea and QPR during his playing days, picked out Brighton as this year’s surprise package.

And while they were beaten in stoppage time by Hull City at the weekend, the ex-England winger is confident the Seagulls remain one of Arsenal’s ‘main challengers’.

‘No disrespect to Arsenal, but the best club for me in the Premier League this season, to watch and for output, is Brighton,’ Wright-Phillips – a Premier League winner with Chelsea in 2006 – explained.

‘Brighton are probably playing the best, but they’re not at the top of the league.

‘It can change and go a different way. I don’t think Arsenal are playing that well, and I don’t think City have played that well, but they’re the two teams that know how to get results when they aren’t playing to the level they know their maximum is.

‘Unfortunately for City, that hasn’t happened in the last four games, which is something they have to deal with and turn around.

‘The Christmas period is the right time to possibly do it, because all the games come quick and fast and the league table can change a dozen times in that time.

‘The main challengers to Arsenal would be Brighton and Manchester City as it stands. They’re the ones with the points on the board.

‘Until people start putting the points on the board, which is turning around, you’re seeing Liverpool sneak back up the table.

‘There will be other challenges as well, but leading into this Christmas period, I would say Arsenal’s challenger right now is Brighton and Manchester City.

In a recent development, ‘Brighton, I think, are the only team to beat both of those two teams and do it nicely as well. It wasn’t a smash and grab.’.

Alexander Isak is closing in on a record held by Mohamed Salah with his latest Liverpool goal.

The Swedish striker did not take long to open the scoring as Liverpool faced Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Bradley Barcola won the ball high up the pitch to set the Reds on the attack and Dominik Szoboszlai teed Isak up to finish from close range.

It was a significant goal for Isak, who has now scored in six consecutive away matches for Liverpool.

It is a feat that very few men have bettered. According to the stat gurus at Opta, no Liverpool player has ever scored in more than seven consecutive away appearances.

Salah is the current record holder, and should Isak find the back of the net in this weekend’s Merseyside derby at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he would equal the Egyptian king’s record. Add another against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on December 5, and he could surpass it.

Prior to the launch of the Premier League, Sam English, John Evans and John Aldridge all scored in seven consecutive away matches.

Salah called time on his Liverpool career at the end of last season, leaving with 257 goals and 123 assists across 442 appearances.

He now plies his trade in Turkey with Trabzonspor, where he has made a bright start to life, tallying 16 goal contributions in his first 17 appearances.

Former England footballer Raheem Sterling, 31, has been handed a suspended prison sentence today.

He was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 18 months, at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court after dangerously driving his Lamborghini and possessing nitrous oxide canisters.

Sterling was also ordered to complete 100 hours of unpaid work and was banned from driving for 24 months.

He had been seen by other motorists inhaling from a balloon while driving his black sports car, swerving in and out of lanes – with one driver ‘shocked’ by what he saw, a court previously heard.

Sterling arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court this morning, wearing a black top and dark trousers.

He has been on unconditional bail and subject to an interim driving ban since he admitted offences in September.

The former Manchester City player had pleaded guilty at the Hampshire court to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on the morning of May 28.

Sterling also admitted possession of six nitrous oxide canisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.

Police body-worn footage of the footballer’s arrest at 9.15am shows him in the crashed car with two canisters on his lap as the officer tells him: ‘You can put that down mate.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The court previously heard witness Christopher Jennings on the M25 called 999 at 7.49am after he was driving in parallel to Sterling’s car and ‘he was shocked by what he saw’.

Sterling scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020.

He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but, after falling out of favour, spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal.

After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the season.

He is currently without a club.

Sterling was made an MBE in the 2021 Queen’s Birthday Honours for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz continued their upward trajectory with the goals in a 3-0 victory over Club Brugge which returned Liverpool to winning ways in the Champions League and got them back on track for a top-eight finish.

Isak took his tally to 10 for the season with a double, his second a wonderful solo effort after shrugging off the attentions of giant centre-back Brandon Mechele to chip over the goalkeeper, while his fellow £100million-plus signing produced a goal equally exquisite.

The pair were the visitors’ best performers in a display which began well, lost its way in the middle, before finishing strongly with two expertly-taken strikes.

After defeat at Fenerbahce last time out it was imperative they responded against the Belgian champions, who had already beaten Inter Milan and PSV Eindhoven, and it was almost a textbook European away performance as they secured the points which lifted them into fifth.

Isak scored for the third successive game after 13 minutes and it was reward for pressuring goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

The Sweden international forced Sommer to misplace a pass which was picked up by Bradley Barcola.

He transferred the ball inside for Dominik Szoboszlai, captaining the team for the first time in the absence of Van Dijk, to cut back for his team-mate to poke home.

Isak was doing a good job of linking play, combining well with Wirtz especially, providing the first line of defence and was also a goal threat, with a snapshot wide from Barcola’s knockdown.

He looks more threatening and seems to have more understanding of Andoni Iraola’s gameplan by the day, but his newly introduced-found resilience will be tested to the full as it seems unthinkable he will not make his third start in a week against Everton.

The form of Wirtz, who scored his sixth goal in five matches for club and country, will also be a concern for the Toffees as the Germany international is brimming with confidence, highlighted by his goal.

When he received Rio Ngumoha’s pass 30 yards out he had only one thought in his mind: take a touch and shoot and he deceived Sommer by rattling a shot in off the goalkeeper’s right-hand post when it was easier to go the other side.

Sources indicate that isak applied the finishing touch, receiving goalkeeper Alisson Becker’s pass with his back to goal 40 yards out. Having shrugged off the lumbering Mechele he also had one intent, but he delivered a wonderful chip to leave Sommer clutching at thin air.

It was a classy finish to a game which had become a grind after the Reds failed to capitalise on their early advantage with Felix Lemarechal and Joaquin Seys having chances.

An injury to Victor Munoz was arguably worse for the hosts as his replacement was Sunday’s man of the match Ngumoha, who early in the second half wriggled into enough space to flash a close-range shot across goal.

Liverpool lost their fluency, although Wirtz and Isak did tee up Szoboszlai for what looked a certain goal before Sommer parried, and after Alisson responded in kind to deny Lemarechal at his near post, Wirtz and Isak delivered the killer blows.

Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s latest-look midfield
